properties.highlight: Hourly cross-country trains link the abbey city of St. Gallen with lakeside Lucerne across the pre-Alps, taking in the Wattwil moorland, the Rapperswil lake dam and the Rothenthurm high bog.

properties.name: Cremallera de Montserrat
properties.highlight: A rack railway climbing the serrated massif to the Benedictine monastery at 720 m: the pilgrims’ way to Catalonia’s black Madonna since 1892.

properties.name: SL Yamaguchi
properties.train: D51 steam with retro Series 35 4000 coaches
properties.highlight: A pacific steam locomotive has hauled this special up the Yamaguchi line to the little castle town of Tsuwano, the “Kyoto of San-in”, since 1979.

properties.name: Fairy Queen Express
properties.train: 1855 Fairy Queen steam locomotive, heritage saloon
properties.highlight: Hauled by the 1855 Fairy Queen, the world’s oldest working steam locomotive, on a heritage run from Delhi out to the tiger country around Alwar.

properties.name: Chemin de fer de La Mure
properties.highlight: Reopened in 2021, this cliffside metre-gauge line hangs on ledges and viaducts high above the turquoise Monteynard reservoir in the Isère.

properties.name: Petit Train de la Rhune
properties.highlight: A 1924 wooden cog train grinds up to the 905 m Basque summit of La Rhune, past pottok ponies and griffon vultures, with the Bay of Biscay spread out below.

properties.name: Beijing–Tianjin Intercity
properties.highlight: China’s first high-speed line, opened for the 2008 Olympics: 350 km/h across the North China Plain, capital to port city in half an hour.

properties.name: Shanghai–Chengdu HSR
properties.highlight: The great east–west artery takes in Nanjing, Wuhan and the Three Gorges country, reaching Sichuan’s capital from the coast in a single day.

properties.name: Hangzhou–Huangshan HSR
properties.highlight: Dubbed China’s most beautiful high-speed line, it slips through tea hills and water towns from West Lake to the granite of Yellow Mountain.

properties.name: Guiyang–Chongqing HSR
properties.highlight: Almost entirely bridge and tunnel, this 2018 line vaults the karst gorges of Guizhou to join two of the mountain south-west’s biggest cities.

properties.name: Lanzhou–Chongqing Railway
properties.highlight: Twenty years in the building through the folded Qinling ranges: hundreds of tunnels that finally gave Gansu a fast way down to the Yangtze.

properties.name: Sarajevo–Maglaj line
properties.highlight: North out of Sarajevo through the Bosna gorge and past Zenica’s steelworks to Maglaj, the surviving stub of the 1947 youth railway to the Sava.

properties.name: Palaiofarsalos–Kalambaka
properties.highlight: The branch to the monasteries in the sky: from the junction at Palaiofarsalos across the Thessalian plain to Kalambaka, beneath the sandstone pillars of Meteora. Athens trains connect here; no through service runs.

properties.name: Shosholoza Meyl Trans-Karoo
properties.train: Class 6E electric & diesel with sleeper cars
properties.highlight: The classic Trans-Karoo run: a night and a day across the semi-desert heart of South Africa from the Highveld gold city down to Table Bay.

properties.name: Central Line
properties.highlight: The German-built Central Line of 1914, a metre-gauge marathon from the Indian Ocean across the plateau to Kigoma on Lake Tanganyika.

properties.name: Baku–Tbilisi–Kars
properties.highlight: The Silk Road revived: opened in 2017, it closes the last gap from the Caspian across the Caucasus to Turkey, a rail bridge between Asia and Europe.

properties.name: Grand Trunk Express
properties.train: LHB sleeper & AC coaches, WAP-7 electric
properties.highlight: Running since 1929, the “GT” hauls down the spine of India through Bhopal and Nagpur to Chennai: 2,180 km in a day and a half.

properties.name: Mandalay–Lashio
properties.train: Myanmar Railways diesel with upper-class coaches
properties.highlight: The Shan hill line crawls up from Mandalay to inch across the Gokteik viaduct: a 1900 American-built steel trestle 100 m above the gorge.

properties.name: Gotthard Panorama Express
properties.train: SBB panorama coaches & lake paddle steamer
properties.highlight: A paddle steamer up Lake Lucerne, then the 1882 Gotthard line’s spirals and the Wassen church seen thrice. Summer only, once daily, seat surcharge.

properties.name: AVE Madrid–Oviedo
properties.highlight: The 2023 Variante de Pajares pierced the Cantabrian wall with a 25 km base tunnel, cutting Asturias’ link to Madrid to about three hours.

properties.name: Alvia Madrid–Badajoz
properties.highlight: High speed reached long-isolated Extremadura in 2022, passing the Roman city of Mérida to the Portuguese border at Badajoz.

properties.name: Tren de la Muerte
properties.highlight: Bolivia’s notorious “Death Train” rattles east from Santa Cruz through Jesuit mission country and the Chiquitano dry forest to the Brazilian frontier.

properties.name: Bosfor Express
properties.highlight: The overnight heir to the Orient Express, crossing the Thracian plain from Istanbul over the Bulgarian border to Sofia as the berths are made up.

properties.name: Albula Railway
properties.highlight: The UNESCO Albula line spirals through helical tunnels and sweeps over the six-arch Landwasser Viaduct, a curved stone bridge running straight into a cliff, on its climb to St. Moritz.

properties.name: Montenvers Railway
properties.highlight: A rack railway since 1908, climbing from Chamonix to a balcony above the Mer de Glace, France’s largest glacier, under the Drus and the Grandes Jorasses.

properties.name: Mont-Blanc Tramway
properties.highlight: France’s highest railway grinds up the flank of Mont Blanc to the Nid d’Aigle at 2,372 m, where the climbers’ route to the summit begins.

properties.name: Schynige Platte Railway
properties.highlight: Vintage 1914 cars grind up an Abt rack to a 2,000 m ridge, with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau lined up across the valley and an alpine garden at the top.

properties.name: Genoa–Casella Railway
properties.highlight: A metre-gauge mountain tram that climbs straight out of central Genoa over three Apennine valleys to the village of Casella, sea views at its back.

properties.name: Nevada Northern Railway
properties.highlight: America’s best-preserved steam-era short line: the “Ghost Train of Old Ely” still runs its 1910 locomotives out of a National Historic Landmark copper yard.

properties.name: Campos do Jordão Railway
properties.highlight: Brazil’s highest railway climbs the Serra da Mantiqueira to the mountain resort of Campos do Jordão at 1,743 m, a metre-gauge line electrified since the 1920s.

properties.name: Zig Zag Railway
properties.highlight: A 19th-century engineering marvel in the Blue Mountains: trains reverse down a rock-cut Z of sandstone viaducts that once carried the main western line off the plateau.

properties.name: AVE Madrid–Murcia
properties.highlight: High speed reached the Segura in December 2022, running Madrid to Murcia via Cuenca and Albacete on a new elevated approach into the palm-country capital.

properties.name: Le Mastrou (Vivarais)
properties.highlight: A metre-gauge steam survivor climbing the granite gorge of the Doux from the Rhône at Tournon to the chestnut country of Lamastre, hauled by 1903 Mallet engines.

properties.name: Chiemsee-Bahn
properties.highlight: The world’s oldest steam tram still in service, an 1887 green Krauss engine that shuttles down to the Chiemsee jetty for the boat to Ludwig II’s island palace.

properties.name: Monte Generoso Railway
properties.highlight: A rack line from the shore of Lake Lugano to a 1,704 m summit whose Mario Botta “Fiore di pietra” lookout takes in the Alps from Monte Rosa to the Apennines.

properties.name: Great Central Railway
properties.highlight: Britain’s only double-track heritage main line, where two steam expresses can pass at speed just as they did on the last main line built towards the Continent.

properties.name: Keighley & Worth Valley Railway
properties.highlight: The branch that starred in the 1970 film “The Railway Children”, steaming up the Brontë moors past Haworth to the mill village of Oxenhope.

properties.name: Kingston Flyer
properties.highlight: A vintage steam service on the old Southland line by Lake Wakatipu, its 1920s Ab Pacific and wooden cars a survivor of New Zealand’s golden age of rail.

properties.name: Himsagar Express
properties.highlight: From the Himalayan foothills at Jammu to the very tip of India at Kanyakumari: about 3,785 km through a dozen states, one of the country’s longest single journeys.

properties.name: Frecciarossa Milan–Reggio Calabria
properties.highlight: The red arrow’s longest domestic run: the length of Italy from Milan down the Tyrrhenian coast to the Strait of Messina at Reggio Calabria.

properties.name: Nightjet Vienna–Rome
properties.highlight: Board in Vienna after dinner, cross the Carinthian Alps and the Venetian plain by night, and wake rolling into Rome, a sleeper between two imperial capitals. From Villach south it runs coupled with the Munich portion as one train.

properties.name: Aurora Winter Train
properties.highlight: The winter run north across frozen Alaska flag-stops for bush residents between Anchorage and Fairbanks, often with the northern lights overhead.

properties.name: TGV inOui
properties.highlight: Races down the Rhône on the LGV Méditerranée, then rides the 2017 Montpellier bypass, the first new stretch of French high-speed line in a decade, to the edge of the Camargue.

properties.name: TGV Lyria
properties.highlight: Via the LGV Rhin-Rhône to the Swiss border at Basel, then along the Aare to Zürich. Paris to Switzerland’s largest city in almost exactly four hours.

properties.name: ICE
properties.highlight: Germany’s busiest long-distance axis, the length of the country from the Elbe to the Isar via Hanover, the Fulda gap and Nuremberg.

properties.name: ICE
properties.highlight: Down the Rhine-Neckar to Mannheim and up into the Swabian capital: a hard-worked spine of the south-west ICE network.

properties.name: Railjet
properties.highlight: Bavaria to the Danube capital along the Westbahn, past Salzburg’s fortress and the baroque abbeys of Upper Austria.

properties.name: EIP Pendolino
properties.highlight: Southwest across the Polish plain via Łódź to Lower Silesia’s handsome market city of Wrocław, threaded with its hundred bridges.

properties.name: Shanghai–Hangzhou HSR
properties.highlight: A 45-minute dash from the metropolis to West Lake, the willow-lined water garden that has drawn Chinese poets for a thousand years.

properties.name: Koralmbahn
properties.highlight: Austria’s game-changer of December 2025: the 33 km Koralm Tunnel cuts Graz–Klagenfurt from nearly three hours to 45 minutes, forging a new Baltic–Adriatic high-speed axis.

properties.name: ICE
properties.highlight: The high-speed link binding Belgium to the Rhineland: past Liège’s soaring Calatrava station and over the language border at Aachen, Charlemagne’s capital, at 300 km/h.

properties.name: Mittenwaldbahn
properties.highlight: Munich to the Tyrol over the Karwendel: the electrified 1912 Mittenwaldbahn climbs from Garmisch through Alpine meadows and horseshoe curves to the Seefeld saddle before dropping into Innsbruck.

properties.name: EuroCity Allgäu
properties.highlight: Electrified in 2020 to speed the Munich–Zürich EuroCitys across the Allgäu past baroque abbeys and Alpine foothills to the island station of Lindau on Lake Constance.

properties.name: Schneebergbahn
properties.highlight: Austria’s highest railway: the red Salamander cog train grinds 1,200 vertical metres from Puchberg to the Hochschneeberg terminus at 1,795 m, the Alps’ balcony over the Vienna basin.

properties.name: Wachaubahn
properties.highlight: Keeps to the north bank of the Danube through the UNESCO Wachau: apricot orchards and terraced vineyards past Dürnstein, where Richard the Lionheart was once held for ransom.

properties.name: Wendelsteinbahn
properties.highlight: Bavaria’s oldest high-mountain railway of 1912 racks up from Brannenburg through tunnels and 25% grades toward the Wendelstein’s summit cave, observatory and panorama over the Inn valley.

properties.name: České dráhy Express
properties.highlight: A winding cross-country run to the grand colonnades of Karlovy Vary, the Bohemian spa where Goethe, Beethoven and half of Europe’s royalty took the waters.

properties.name: Erzbergbahn
properties.highlight: The “Semmering of the ore”: a heritage line over the 1,204 m Präbichl pass under the terraced Erzberg, the ochre iron mountain worked for over 1,300 years.

properties.name: Oravița–Anina Railway
properties.highlight: The “Banat Semmering” of 1863. Romania’s first mountain railway spirals through 14 tunnels and over 10 viaducts up the Aninei gorges, a masterwork of Habsburg engineering.

properties.name: Oslo–Göteborg
properties.highlight: The busiest cross-border run in Scandinavia: down Norway’s Østfold Line to the frontier at Kornsjø, then through Dalsland’s forests and lakes to Sweden’s second city; a new fast line is planned to halve the time.

properties.name: Oslo–Stockholm
properties.highlight: Two Scandinavian capitals across the forests and lakes of Värmland, via Kongsvinger and Karlstad on Lake Vänern: a near-five-hour run that new open-access operators are racing to cut.

properties.name: Pustertalbahn
properties.highlight: Follows the Puster Valley below the Dolomites from the Brenner line at Fortezza past Bruneck and the Three Peaks, crossing into Austria at Innichen to run on to Lienz in East Tyrol.

properties.name: Salzkammergutbahn
properties.highlight: Austria’s lake district by rail: from Attnang-Puchheim along the Traunsee past the imperial spa of Bad Ischl to the shore opposite Hallstatt, the picture-postcard village mirrored in its emerald lake.

properties.name: Meråkerbanen
properties.highlight: Up the Stjørdal valley from the Trondheim fjord to the Swedish border at Storlien: freshly electrified in 2024, the northern rail gateway between Norway and Sweden toward Östersund.

properties.name: Treno Gottardo
properties.highlight: The everyday Gotthard panorama train: hourly IRs over the 1882 mountain line’s spiral tunnels, no surcharge, from Basel or Zürich to Locarno’s palms.

properties.name: Train de l’Aubrac
properties.highlight: One daily train across the empty heart of France: over Garabit’s red Eiffel viaduct, the Truyère gorges and the Causses down to the Med. Six hours, change at Neussargues.

properties.name: Ligne des Horlogers
properties.highlight: The Watchmakers’ Line: out of Besançon and up the Doubs gorges to 1,000 m Jura plateaus, crossing into Switzerland at Le Locle for watch-capital La Chaux-de-Fonds.

properties.name: Fichtelbergbahn
properties.highlight: Saxon narrow-gauge steam, every day of the year: 750 mm VII K locomotives hauling green coaches 238 m uphill to Oberwiesenthal, Germany’s highest town.

properties.name: Usedomer Bäderbahn
properties.highlight: The imperial spa line: along Usedom’s beaches from Züssow over the Peene bridge to Ahlbeck’s pier, then across the border into Świnoujście.

properties.name: Tarka Line
properties.highlight: Along the Taw through Henry Williamson’s Tarka the Otter country: Devon’s surviving branch line winding from Exeter’s cathedral city to Barnstaple.

properties.name: Hel Peninsula Line
properties.highlight: A railway down a sandbar: 34 km along the Hel spit, at points 200 m wide, open Baltic one side and lagoon the other. Packed solid every Polish summer.

properties.name: Bastia–Calvi
properties.highlight: The Trinighellu’s Balagne arm: inland from Bastia to Ponte-Leccia, then down to a beach-hugging crawl from Île-Rousse to Calvi’s citadel.

properties.name: InterCity
properties.highlight: Across the midland bogs and Mayo’s drumlin country to Clew Bay: Ireland’s western rails since 1866, with Croagh Patrick rising past the buffer stops.

properties.name: Midland Main Line
properties.highlight: St Pancras’s own intercity: the Midland Main Line under Barlow’s great arch, up through Bedford and Leicester to Nottingham, Britain’s last classic trunk to join the atlas.

properties.name: Great Eastern Main Line
properties.highlight: “Norwich in 90”: East Anglia’s main line across Constable country with its all-new Swiss-built FLIRT fleet. A whole English region in one green run.

properties.name: Highland Main Line
properties.highlight: Over Druimuachdar Pass at 452 m, the highest main line in Britain, threading the Cairngorms from the capital to the Highland capital.

properties.name: West Highland Line to Oban
properties.highlight: The West Highland Line’s other arm: splitting at Crianlarich for Loch Awe, Kilchurn Castle’s ruin and the Hebrides ferry port of Oban.

properties.name: Welsh Marches Line
properties.highlight: The great spine outside England’s trunk lines: Cardiff to Manchester up the castle-studded Welsh border through Abergavenny, Ludlow and Shrewsbury.

properties.name: InterCity
properties.highlight: Ireland’s longest ride: off the Cork line at Mallow and west past Killarney’s lakes to Tralee, with Kerry and the Atlantic at the end of the rails.

properties.name: Brighton Main Line
properties.highlight: Victorian London’s dash to the sea, once home of the all-Pullman Brighton Belle, and still under the hour from Victoria to the pier and the Lanes.

properties.name: Edinburgh–Glasgow Express
properties.highlight: Scotland’s busiest corridor since 1842: four electric expresses an hour between its two great cities over the Falkirk high route.

properties.name: Hope Valley Line
properties.highlight: Straight through the Peak District: Edale, Kinder Scout and the Hope valley between England’s steel and cotton cities. The hikers’ line.

properties.name: InterCity
properties.highlight: Into Finnish Lakeland by the tunnel-heavy Jämsä gorge cutoff, to Alvar Aalto’s university city among a thousand lakes.

properties.name: South Western Main Line
properties.highlight: Waterloo’s main line to the sea: Winchester’s cathedral close, Southampton’s ocean-liner docks, Bournemouth sands and the Jurassic Coast at Weymouth.

properties.name: Cumbrian Coast Line
properties.highlight: England’s forgotten coastal railway: the Irish Sea one side, the Lakeland fells the other, all the way round from Hadrian’s city to shipbuilding Barrow.

properties.name: InterCity
properties.highlight: Fourteen direct ICs a day to Finland’s sunniest city, down the Ostrobothnian flats to Vaasa and the UNESCO Kvarken archipelago.

properties.name: Borders Railway
properties.highlight: The Waverley Route reborn: Britain’s longest railway reopening in a century (2015), winding out of Edinburgh to Walter Scott’s Abbotsford.

properties.name: Dalabanan
properties.highlight: To Dalarna, Sweden’s folklore heart: Lake Siljan, Leksand’s midsummer poles and the Vasaloppet town of Mora, where the Inlandsbanan begins.

properties.name: Conwy Valley Line
properties.highlight: From the pier at Llandudno up the Conwy gorge into Snowdonia’s slate mountains, meeting the Ffestiniog steam trains at Blaenau: coast to crag in an hour.

properties.name: Jūrmala Line
properties.highlight: Latvia’s beach train: across the Lielupe to the villas and pines of Jūrmala’s resort strip, then the bog boardwalks of Ķemeri national park.

properties.name: Western Rail Corridor
properties.highlight: The Western Rail Corridor, reopened in 2010 after 34 years: north from Limerick through Ennis and the stone-walled edge of the Burren to Galway Bay, west of the Shannon the whole way and never near Dublin.

properties.name: Tyne Valley Line
properties.highlight: One of the world’s first cross-country railways (1838), shadowing Hadrian’s Wall from the Tyne to the Solway, the Roman frontier out the window.

properties.name: InterRegio
properties.highlight: Wallachia to the old Moldavian capital: Romania’s busiest eastern corridor, hours of steppe and vineyards ending in university-city Iași.

properties.name: ITX-Maum · Donghae Line
properties.highlight: Korea’s newest line: the last east-coast gap closed on New Year’s Day 2025, and now one train runs the whole East Sea shore, Busan to Gangneung.

properties.name: Güney Kurtalan Ekspresi
properties.highlight: The third of Turkey’s great eastern sleepers: off the Anatolian plateau to Diyarbakır’s black basalt walls and the Tigris, ending at railhead Kurtalan.

properties.name: Limited Express Shinano
properties.highlight: Tilting up the Kiso Valley: the old Nakasendō post road’s gorge and pass country on the classic mountain road to Nagano.

properties.name: Limited Express Kuroshio
properties.highlight: Around the Kii Peninsula with the Pacific at the window: Shirahama’s sands, Honshu’s southernmost cape and the Kumano pilgrim coast.

properties.name: Limited Express Nanpu
properties.highlight: Across the Great Seto Bridge, then up the Yoshino river’s Oboke and Koboke gorges, tilting over the island spine to Kochi.

properties.name: Toros Ekspresi
properties.highlight: Heir to the Taurus Express of Agatha Christie fame: down the Cilician Gates on Baghdad Railway engineering to the cotton plains of Adana.

properties.name: IRN Corona
properties.highlight: Romania’s classic night loop: asleep through Székely Land and the Maramureș foothills, waking at the far northwestern corner of the country.

properties.name: Limited Express Shiokaze
properties.highlight: Along the Seto Inland Sea’s island-studded shore to Dōgo Onsen, Japan’s oldest hot spring. Shikoku’s busiest express, tilting the whole way.

properties.name: KTX Jeolla Line
properties.highlight: Off the Honam high-speed line at Iksan and down the Jeolla branch: hanok-roofed Jeonju, Suncheon’s gardens and the Expo harbour at Yeosu.

properties.name: BDZ Fast Train
properties.highlight: Capital to the Danube: through the Iskar gorge, across the Pleven plain, down to Ruse’s Habsburg-flavoured riverfront and the bridge to Romania.

properties.name: InterRegio
properties.highlight: The Moldavia main line north through Bacău and Roman to Suceava, jumping-off point for Bukovina’s painted monasteries.

properties.name: Limited Express Kamui
properties.highlight: Hokkaido’s busiest shuttle: near-hourly across the Ishikari plain to Asahikawa, the doorway to Biei’s hills and Daisetsuzan’s peaks.

properties.name: Limited Express Okhotsk
properties.highlight: One of Japan’s last great remote expresses: over the Kitami Pass through forest-empty interior to the drift-ice coast of the Sea of Okhotsk.

properties.name: Limited Express Sōya
properties.highlight: One return working a day to Japan’s northernmost station: five hours up the Sōya Main Line to Wakkanai, in sight of Sakhalin on a clear day.

properties.name: Missouri River Runner
properties.highlight: Twice a day along the wide Missouri: Hermann’s German wine town, the capitol at Jefferson City and ragtime Sedalia between the two big cities.

properties.name: VIA Jonquière
properties.highlight: A flag-stop wilderness train: nine hours through Laurentides lake country few roads reach, to the Saguenay fjord railhead of Jonquière.

properties.name: Railjet Wien–Lienz
properties.highlight: Osttirol’s capital link restored: two railjets a day over the Semmering, through the new Koralm tunnel and up the Drau valley. A child of the Dec 2025 timetable.

properties.name: Jižní expres
properties.highlight: Czechia’s first 200 km/h running: the rebuilt Fourth Corridor past Tábor’s Hussite hilltop to the Budweiser city, a record 85 minutes on the fastest Pendolinos.

properties.name: München–Innsbruck
properties.highlight: The Brenner corridor’s northern approach: out of Munich, across the Inn at Rosenheim, into Tyrol at Kufstein and up the valley beneath the Karwendel wall.

properties.name: Railjet · Deutsches Eck
properties.highlight: Tyrol to Salzburg the fast way, through Bavaria: Austrian expresses cut the German corner nonstop via Rosenheim, Alps on the horizon the whole run.

properties.name: EC Transalpin
properties.highlight: One train, one panorama car, half the Alps: Zurich to Graz over the Arlberg, past Zell am See, the Ennstal and the Gesäuse gates. The day-long EuroCity people ride for the window.

properties.name: IC Hamburg–Köln
properties.highlight: Germany’s busiest conventional corridor: ports to Ruhr through Bremen, Münster and five more big cities. Twice an hour, and no high-speed line in sight.

properties.name: IC 1
properties.highlight: Switzerland’s flagship express and spine of the clockface timetable: Zurich to Geneva across the Mittelland, Bern and Lausanne on the way, every half hour.

properties.name: REX Wien–Bratislava
properties.highlight: Europe’s closest capital pair, an hour apart on the 1848 Marchegg line across the Morava floodplain: two countries, one commuter corridor.

properties.name: EuroCity Hungaria corridor
properties.highlight: The Danube-bend main line: EuroCities every two hours sweeping past Štúrovo and the great river’s knee at Visegrád into Budapest.

properties.name: alex München–Praha
properties.highlight: The only direct Munich–Prague train: a famously unhurried crossing of the Bavarian Forest and Bohemia while the corridor awaits its wires.

properties.name: EuroNight Praha–Zürich
properties.highlight: The Czech–Swiss night link revived in 2023: the Elbe sandstone gorge at dusk, the Rhine plain at dawn, Zurich by breakfast.

properties.name: EuroCity Budapest–Zagreb
properties.highlight: The only Hungary–Croatia day train: along Balaton’s southern shore, over the Drava at Gyékényes and down through Zagorje to Zagreb.

properties.name: EC Hornád
properties.highlight: Budapest’s only direct reach into eastern Slovakia: the little EuroCity that grows at Miskolc, bound for Košice’s Gothic cathedral square.

properties.name: IC Kraków–Wrocław
properties.highlight: Poland’s two great tourist cities linked across industrial Silesia on the 1847 Upper Silesian Railway, the mesh line no Warsaw-bound train covers.

properties.name: IC Budapest–Szeged
properties.highlight: Hourly ICs across the Great Plain to Hungary’s paprika capital and its vast Votive Church. The southern spoke of the MÁV intercity star.

properties.name: Wolsztyn Steam
properties.highlight: Europe’s last everyday steam: commuters behind a 1948 Pt47 out of the working Wolsztyn roundhouse. An ordinary ticket, an extraordinary train.

properties.name: IC 3
properties.highlight: The approach every Glacier and Bernina rider actually takes: along Lake Zurich and the Walensee’s cliff wall to Chur, where the narrow gauge begins.

properties.name: IC Poznań–Szczecin
properties.highlight: Continuation of the Warsaw expresses to the Baltic’s big absent city: Szczecin’s Prussian boulevards and the gateway to Świnoujście.

properties.name: Szeged–Békéscsaba railway
properties.highlight: Line 135 strikes east across the Great Hungarian Plain through Hódmezővásárhely and Orosháza; the rails carry on past Békéscsaba to Salonta, over a border drawn in 1920.

properties.name: Poznań–Piła railway
properties.highlight: Built in 1879 to hook Poznań onto the Prussian Eastern Railway; a recent rebuild cut about fifteen minutes off the run north through Chodzież to Piła.

properties.name: Main-Weser Railway
properties.highlight: One of Germany’s first trunk railways, opened in stages between 1849 and 1852 through Gießen and Marburg; its 160 km/h ceiling is only reachable on the southern half.

properties.name: Rome–Sulmona–Pescara railway
properties.highlight: Rome to the Adriatic the hard way, over the Apennines by Tivoli, the drained Fucino basin at Avezzano and Sulmona, where the Transiberiana d’Italia branches into the Abruzzo highlands.

properties.name: Ionian Railway
properties.highlight: Six hours down the instep and toe of Italy, from Taranto by Metaponto, Sibari and Crotone to the Strait of Messina; the sections were joined into one railway in 1875.

properties.name: Zafra–Huelva railway
properties.highlight: Built in 1889 to carry Sierra de Aracena ore down to the quays at Huelva, and still crossing it past halts named for villages miles from the line: Jabugo, Almonaster, Valdelamusa.

properties.name: Stångådalsbanan
properties.highlight: Four separate railways stitched into one 235 kilometre run across Småland; the last section opened in 1902, and only since 1996 has the trip been possible without changing trains.

properties.name: Poitiers–La Rochelle railway
properties.highlight: The Paris TGVs peel off at Poitiers and finish on this line, opened to Niort in 1856 and to La Rochelle the year after: ninety minutes across the Poitou plain to the Atlantic.

properties.name: Bordeaux–Hendaye railway
properties.highlight: Dead straight down the Landes pine forest to the Basque coast; the rails left Bordeaux in 1841 and took until 1864 to reach the Spanish border at Irun.

properties.name: Amiens–Rouen railway
properties.highlight: Opened complete on 18 April 1867 rather than in stages, and still the cross country way from Picardy into Normandy by Poix-de-Picardie, Abancourt and Serqueux.

properties.name: Halle–Halberstadt railway
properties.highlight: The Halle end of the line that reached Vienenburg in 1872, ninety two kilometres by Könnern, Sandersleben and Aschersleben to Halberstadt on the northern edge of the Harz.

properties.name: Lower Left Rhine Railway
properties.highlight: The Rhine’s quiet left bank to the Dutch border: Kempen, Geldern, the pilgrim town of Kevelaer and Goch, on rails that reached Kleve on 1 March 1863.

properties.name: Manresa–Lleida railway
properties.highlight: Inland Catalonia the slow way, over the Segarra plateau by Calaf and Cervera; the first trains ran into Lleida in 1860 while the coastal route through Valls took the traffic.

properties.name: Turin–Genoa railway
properties.highlight: Five years of tunnelling under the Apennines opened this line in December 1853, and the 3.3 km Giovi tunnel at its summit was then the longest in the world.

properties.name: Domodossola–Milan railway
properties.highlight: The Simplon’s Italian approach, down the Toce and along the western shore of Lake Maggiore by Stresa and Arona; the rails reached Domodossola in 1888.

properties.name: Verona–Bologna railway
properties.highlight: Thirty seven years to cross the Po plain: begun at Bologna in 1887, over the river at Ostiglia in 1911 and finished into Verona on 1 February 1924. Fifty two minutes now.

properties.name: Milan–Bologna classic line
properties.highlight: The old road through Emilia by Lodi, Piacenza, Parma, Reggio and Modena, single track when it opened in 1861 and doubled by 1894; the Frecce take the high speed line beside it.

properties.name: Dresden–Görlitz railway
properties.highlight: Saxony end to end through Bautzen and the Lusatian hills, opened in stages from November 1845 and formally complete on 1 September 1847.

properties.name: Vendsyssel Line
properties.highlight: The last railway in Jutland, through Brønderslev and Hjørring to the ferry quays at Frederikshavn; it reached Aalborg itself in 1879, when the Limfjord bridge opened.

properties.name: Zalaegerszeg–Boba railway
properties.highlight: Up the Zala valley on rails the Transdanubian local company laid: Boba to Ukk in January 1889, on through Zalaegerszeg in October 1890, and now the first leg of the line to Slovenia.

properties.name: Udine–Trieste railway
properties.highlight: Friuli to the Adriatic through Gorizia and out along the Carso above Miramare; the last two sections opened three days apart in October 1860.

properties.name: Prato–Bologna Direttissima
properties.highlight: The 1934 Direttissima under the Apennines: an 18.5 km base tunnel, then the second longest in the world, and 180 km/h where the old line over the pass managed 75.

properties.name: Ljubljana–Jesenice railway
properties.highlight: The Slovenian half of the Rudolf Railway, opened complete on 14 December 1870, up the Sava by Škofja Loka and Kranj to the mouth of the Karawanks tunnel.

properties.name: Gotha–Leinefelde railway
properties.highlight: Forty two minutes across the Thuringian Basin through Bad Langensalza and Mühlhausen, opened in 1870 and now rebuilt for 160 km/h.

properties.name: Northwest Line
properties.highlight: Zealand from Roskilde out to the Great Belt at Kalundborg, opened on 30 December 1874 and doubled as far as Holbæk in 2014.

properties.name: Oldenburg–Osnabrück railway
properties.highlight: Across the Oldenburg moors and the Artland by Cloppenburg and Quakenbrück; opened as far as Quakenbrück in October 1875 and through to Osnabrück on 15 November 1876.

properties.name: Saalbahn
properties.highlight: Forty two minutes up the Saale gorge from Jena by Kahla, Orlamünde and Rudolstadt, on a line opened through to Saalfeld on 30 April 1874.

properties.name: Plovdiv–Karlovo railway
properties.highlight: North out of Plovdiv to the Rose Valley at Karlovo under the Balkan range, sixty one kilometres opened on 28 September 1933.

properties.name: Kinnekullebanan
properties.highlight: Four small railways stitched round the flat-topped hill of Kinnekulle by Lidköping and Mariestad, the last piece laid in 1910 and the whole of it regauged to standard by 1953.

properties.name: Lahn Valley Railway
properties.highlight: The Lahn from Wetzlar down to the Rhine through Weilburg, Limburg, Nassau and the spa at Bad Ems; opened in three pieces and finished on 10 January 1863.

properties.name: Civitanova Marche–Fabriano railway
properties.highlight: Off the Adriatic at Civitanova and up the Chienti and Potenza valleys by Macerata and Matelica; begun in 1884 at the far end and joined up in 1888.

properties.name: Lemvigbanen
properties.highlight: A Danish local line that never belonged to the state: Vemb to the fishing port of Thyborøn by Lemvig and Harboøre, finished on 1 November 1899 and still privately run.

properties.name: Hohenlohebahn
properties.highlight: Up the Kocher from Heilbronn through Schwäbisch Hall to Crailsheim; the first half opened in August 1862 and the rest waited until 10 December 1867.

properties.name: Frankenwaldbahn
properties.highlight: The climb over the Frankenwald from the Main valley to the Thuringian border at Probstzella by Kronach and Ludwigsstadt, finished in October 1885 and steep enough to need banking engines.

properties.name: Delmenhorst–Hesepe railway
properties.highlight: The Oldenburg south line through Vechta and Lohne, built in four pieces between 1888 and 1 May 1900, and still eighty kilometres an hour the whole way.

properties.name: Avezzano–Roccasecca railway
properties.highlight: Up the Liri from Roccasecca by Arce, Sora and Balsorano into the Fucino basin; eighteen years from the first section in 1884 to the last on 20 August 1902.

properties.name: Mátészalka–Záhony railway
properties.highlight: Opened on 27 September 1905 as a local line from Nagykároly to Csap; the border of 1920 cut it in three, and this is the Hungarian piece, out to the frontier at Záhony.

properties.name: Binsui Line
properties.highlight: The eastern arm of the old Chinese Eastern Railway, running provisionally from November 1901 and opened properly on 14 July 1903; ten hours from Harbin to the Russian border at Suifenhe.

properties.name: Jōban Line
properties.highlight: Tokyo to Sendai up the Pacific coast, inland of the Shinkansen: complete on 1 April 1905, and reopened right through Fukushima in March 2020 after nine years shut.

properties.name: Golești–Câmpulung railway
properties.highlight: Inaugurated on 21 June 1887 and derailed two months later between Mihăești and Stâlpeni; still an hour and a half up the Râul Târgului to Câmpulung.

properties.name: Hatvan–Újszász railway
properties.highlight: Down the Zagyva through the Jaszsag, opened on 10 March 1873 with four stations on it and electrified a century later in 1975.

properties.name: TGV Paris–Luxembourg
properties.highlight: The only direct rail link between the two capitals: 320 km/h across Champagne on the LGV Est, then down the Moselle past Metz’s golden cathedral.

properties.name: Nomad Krono+
properties.highlight: Normandy’s trunk from Saint-Lazare: Lisieux, Caen and Bayeux of the Tapestry, out along the Cotentin to the great naval harbour of Cherbourg.

properties.name: Nomad Krono
properties.highlight: The Impressionists’ line down the Seine: Vernon for Giverny, Rouen’s spires, and the ferro-concrete UNESCO city at the river’s mouth.

properties.name: European Sleeper
properties.highlight: The night train that replaced the lost Nightjet: Paris to Berlin via Brussels three times a week since March 2026, the open-access sleeper’s boldest route yet.

properties.name: Intercités
properties.highlight: The Atlantic link that skips Paris: marshes of the Vendée, La Rochelle’s towers and the Charente to Bordeaux. Ridership has doubled, and it is contracted to 2036.

properties.name: Intercités
properties.highlight: France’s great west–east diagonal, no Paris required: the Loire at Angers and Tours, Bourges’ cathedral, then Roanne and the Lyon hills.

properties.name: Alvia
properties.highlight: Gauge-changing Alvias to the Basque coast: the 2022 Burgos high-speed line, Vitoria’s green ring and the belle-époque bay of La Concha at the end.

properties.name: Alvia
properties.highlight: Off the high-speed line at Palencia and over the 1866 Reinosa pass, then a mountain descent to the Cantabrian Sea and Santander’s curved bay.

properties.name: Avant Eje Atlántico
properties.highlight: Galicia’s rebuilt Atlantic spine: 250 km/h between the rías with Santiago de Compostela halfway. The north–south line Madrid’s radial map forgets.

properties.name: TGV Rhin-Rhône
properties.highlight: France’s only province-to-province LGV: Burgundy to Alsace without a glance at Paris, Dijon and Belfort on the way to the cathedral city.

properties.name: TGV Paris–Brest
properties.highlight: To Brittany’s Atlantic tip: the 2017 LGV to Rennes, then the granite north coast by Saint-Brieuc and Morlaix’s viaduct to the naval roadstead of Brest.

properties.name: TGV Paris–Quimper
properties.highlight: Brittany’s other arm: the same 2017 high speed line to Rennes, where the Brest and Quimper halves of the train part company, then south to the Morbihan coast by Vannes, Auray and Lorient to Quimper in Finistère.

properties.name: Intercités de Nuit
properties.highlight: The Pyrenean pilgrim night train: out of Austerlitz every evening on the classic line through Poitiers and Dax, waking beneath the mountains at Lourdes.

properties.name: Intercity Tirreno
properties.highlight: The Tyrrhenian artery the high-speed network bypasses: Maremma’s coast, Pisa, the marble Apuans and the whole Riviera di Levante into Genoa.

properties.name: Milano–Tirano
properties.highlight: Lake Como’s eastern shore from the train window: Varenna, then the vineyard terraces of the Valtellina to Tirano, where the Bernina Express waits.

properties.name: Bari–Matera
properties.highlight: The only railway to the Sassi: a 950 mm oddity climbing the Murgia plateau from Bari to cave-city Matera, every visitor’s first sight of Basilicata.

properties.name: Avant Madrid–Toledo
properties.highlight: Thirty-three minutes off the Seville high-speed line to the city on the Tagus bend: El Greco’s Toledo as a Madrid day trip.

properties.name: Mr Henderson’s Railway
properties.highlight: Up the Serranía de Ronda from Gibraltar bay: the British-built 1892 line that is Mr Henderson’s railway proper, Algeciras to the Bobadilla plain, ending today at Antequera Santa Ana’s high-speed interchange.

properties.name: Rodalies R3
properties.highlight: Climbs from Barcelona to 1,494 m at Toses, the roof of the Spanish network, to meet the Yellow Train across the platform at Latour-de-Carol.

properties.name: Intercidades
properties.highlight: Across the Tagus and into the cork-oak Alentejo: ninety minutes from Lisbon to Évora’s Roman temple and bone chapel.

properties.name: Linha do Algarve
properties.highlight: The Algarve coast end to end: Portimão, Silves’ red castle, Faro and the Ria Formosa lagoons out to Vila Real de Santo António on the Guadiana. Every summer visitor’s slow shuttle.

properties.name: Thrace InterCity
properties.highlight: Greece’s only train across Thrace: 440 km laid in 1896 for the Salonika–Constantinople railway, threading the Nestos gorge between Drama and Xanthi.

properties.name: Pamukkale Ekspresi
properties.highlight: Heir of the Haydarpaşa night express: 418 km across the Aegean interior via Kütahya, Afyon and Dinar, down to Denizli’s white travertine country.

properties.name: Osoblažka
properties.highlight: Czechia’s last public narrow gauge: 760 mm and 102 curves in 20 km (including the network’s sharpest, at 75 m radius), dawdling across Silesia at 40 km/h.

properties.name: Żnin District Railway
properties.highlight: A 600 mm minirailway from 1894 chuffing 12 km through Pałuki to the Iron Age lake fort of Biskupin, where archaeologists commute by narrow gauge.

properties.name: Nadmorska Kolej Wąskotorowa
properties.highlight: Opened 1896 and still packing 150,000 riders a summer: metre-gauge cars amble from Gryfice to the Baltic cliffs, Poland’s last coastal narrow gauge.

properties.name: Upper Silesian Narrow Gauge
properties.highlight: Running since 1853, the world’s oldest continuously operating narrow gauge: 785 mm industrial track turned heritage line across the Silesian coalfield.

properties.name: Mocănița Huțulca
properties.highlight: Bucovina’s oldest mocănița, laid in 1888 for a Munich sawmill: the Huțulca puffs 12 km up the Moldovița valley behind a Reșița-built 764 steam engine.

properties.name: Mocănița Sovata
properties.highlight: From the spa resort of Sovata a 1949 Chrzanów steam engine hauls open cars to Câmpu Cetății, on a rescued shard of the 82 km Târgu Mureș–Praid line of 1915.

properties.name: Katakolo–Olympia Train
properties.highlight: Greece’s first provincial railway (1882–83) reborn as a cruise shuttle: a metre-gauge railcar links Katakolo’s quay with the sanctuary of Ancient Olympia.

properties.name: Orava Forest Railway
properties.highlight: Built by POWs in 1915–18 to haul timber: the surviving 3.5 km climbs from Tanečník to Sedlo Beskyd on a five-switchback staircase unique in Europe.

properties.name: Posázavský Pacifik
properties.highlight: Prague’s “Pacific”, the tramps’ weekend railway of the 1920s: ledges above the Vltava and Sázava canyons and the 41 m Žampach viaduct on the way to Čerčany.

properties.name: 6 Eylül Ekspresi
properties.highlight: Heir of the Bandırma boat trains that sped İzmir–Istanbul travellers to the Marmara ferries: relaunched in 2023, 341 km via Manisa and Balıkesir.

properties.name: Northern Trans-Iranian
properties.highlight: The Trans-Iranian’s UNESCO-listed northern arm: night sleepers spiral down the Alborz over the Veresk bridge, from Tehran’s desert rim to the Caspian plain.

properties.name: Weißeritztalbahn
properties.highlight: Germany’s oldest working public narrow gauge (1882): 750 mm steam daily through the Rabenauer Grund gorge and past Malter dam, 350 m up into the Ore Mountains to Kipsdorf.

properties.name: Lößnitzgrundbahn
properties.highlight: Daily steam on Dresden’s doorstep since 1884: out of Radebeul’s villa streets into the wooded Lößnitzgrund, past Moritzburg’s moated hunting palace to little Radeburg.

properties.name: Harzquerbahn
properties.highlight: HSB’s metre-gauge trunk across the Harz: 2-10-2 tank engines storm out of Nordhausen up the Zorge valley to Drei Annen Hohne, the junction where the Brocken steam begins.

properties.name: Berner Oberland-Bahn
properties.highlight: Jungfrau gateway since 1890: from Interlaken Ost the BOB splits at Zweilütschinen. One arm goes to Lauterbrunnen; this one climbs to Grindelwald under the Eiger’s north face.

properties.name: Waldviertelbahn
properties.highlight: NÖVOG’s 760 mm Südast winds from Gmünd through the granite-and-pine Waldviertel to Groß Gerungs, summer steam grinding round horseshoe bends and over stone viaducts.

properties.name: Murtalbahn
properties.highlight: Austria’s second-longest narrow gauge (1894) follows the young Mur 64 km from Unzmarkt to Tamsweg: 70 km/h diesels on weekdays, steam specials all summer.

properties.name: Chemins de fer du Jura
properties.highlight: Metre gauge across the Franches-Montagnes plateau: horse pastures and firs at 1,000 m from watch-town La Chaux-de-Fonds to Saignelégier, then a wooded ravine descent to Glovelier.

properties.name: Brohltalbahn
properties.highlight: The Vulkan-Expreß ambles at Tempo 20 from the Rhine at Brohl 400 m up into the volcanic Eifel, on metre gauge laid in 1901 to carry the region’s tuff and phonolite.

properties.name: Drachenfelsbahn
properties.highlight: Germany’s oldest rack railway (1883) climbs 220 m in eight minutes from Königswinter past Schloss Drachenburg to the Drachenfels ruin above the Rhine, Siegfried’s dragon mountain.

properties.name: Borkumer Kleinbahn
properties.highlight: Timed to the tide: Borkum’s 900 mm railway (1888) meets every ferry at the Reede pier and rolls 7 km along the dike into the North Sea island’s town.

properties.name: Reblaus-Express
properties.highlight: Named after the phylloxera louse: a heritage diesel with a wine-tavern car trundles from Retz’s vine terraces to the Thaya loop at Drosendorf, weekends May to October.

properties.name: Blonay–Chamby Museum Railway
properties.highlight: Switzerland’s first museum railway (running since 1968): Belle Époque steam and electrics cross the Baye de Clarens viaduct high above Lake Geneva on 3 km of 1902 branch line.

properties.name: Preßnitztalbahn
properties.highlight: Torn up in 1986, relaid 1992–2000 by volunteers: Saxon IV K tanks once more steam the upper Preßnitz valley from Steinbach to Jöhstadt on weekends through the year.

properties.name: Steyrtal-Museumsbahn
properties.highlight: Austria’s oldest 760 mm line (1889): ÖGEG steam ambles down the green Steyr valley from Steyr Lokalbahnhof to Grünburg on summer weekends. Bosnian gauge as it began.

properties.name: Wangerooger Inselbahn
properties.highlight: Deutsche Bahn’s only narrow gauge: the tide writes the timetable as diesels haul ferry passengers across the salt marsh from Westanleger pier to car-free Wangerooge village.

properties.name: KTM ETS3
properties.highlight: Electric at last to the peninsula’s tip: since December 2025 the ETS3 EMUs run Kuala Lumpur–Johor Bahru direct, ending a nine-year rail gap to Malaysia’s second city.

properties.name: Mutiara Timur
properties.highlight: Java’s eastern express since 1973, tracing the north coast past Probolinggo before winding through coffee country to the Bali ferry pier at Ketapang.

properties.name: Rajabasa
properties.highlight: South Sumatra’s all-day economy flagship: nine and a half hours and dozens of halts through rubber, coal and pepper country from Palembang to Bandar Lampung.

properties.name: Sribilah Utama
properties.highlight: North Sumatra’s mainline stalwart since 1978, rolling out of Medan across plantation flatlands to the railhead town of Rantau Prapat.

properties.name: Hotan–Ruoqiang Railway
properties.highlight: The 2022 desert line that closed the world’s first rail loop around a sand sea: 825 km along the Taklamakan’s southern rim on viaducts built to let the dunes blow through.

properties.name: Chuanqing Railway
properties.highlight: China’s mountain railway to fairyland: 200 km/h from the Chengdu plain up the Min valley to Huangshengguan, the new gateway station for Jiuzhaigou and Huanglong.

properties.name: Harbin–Mohe Snow Country Train
properties.highlight: The “Snow Country Train” heads 17 hours north to China’s northernmost station at Mohe, where −40 °C winters, frost forests and the odd aurora reward the ride.

properties.name: Binzhou Railway
properties.highlight: The Chinese Eastern Railway’s west arm, working since 1902: over the Greater Khingan to the Russian border at Manzhouli, where the Trans-Manchurian crosses to Zabaikalsk.

properties.name: Jingha Railway
properties.highlight: Its Tangshan–Tianjin end opened in 1881 as the Kaiping Tramway and is the oldest railway still working in China; the Z15 runs the whole 1,249 km overnight in ten hours.

properties.name: S-train (Namdo Ocean)
properties.highlight: Since September 2025 the S-train sweeps the whole south coast from Busan to Mokpo, crossing the brand-new Boseong–Imseongri line past tea fields and tidal bays.

properties.name: Isan Watthana
properties.highlight: Thailand’s smartest sleeper: Chinese-built berths glide out of Bangkok at dusk and wake along the Mun River in Ubon Ratchathani, deep in southern Isan.

properties.name: Sabah State Railway
properties.highlight: Borneo’s only railway, opened to Tenom in 1905: a metre-gauge survivor that squeezes through the roaring Padas Gorge on its jungle climb inland.

properties.name: Gajayana
properties.train: KAI New Generation executive & luxury coaches
properties.highlight: KAI’s flagship sleeper since 1999 leaves Jakarta after dark and skirts Java’s southern volcanoes to reach highland Malang in time for breakfast.

properties.name: A-train (Jeongseon Arirang)
properties.highlight: The Arirang-themed A-train leaves the Jungang main line at Jecheon and threads the Jeongseon canyon to Auraji, where two mountain torrents meet.

properties.name: Rail Cruise Haerang
properties.highlight: Korea’s only sleeper cruise: three days around the entire peninsula from Seoul (Suncheon Bay, Busan, Gyeongju, the Jeongdongjin sunrise), with the train as the hotel.

properties.name: G-train (West Gold)
properties.highlight: The West Gold train ambles down the Janghang line’s tidal-flat coast, foot baths steaming on board, with Daecheon beach and the Geum estuary out the window.

properties.name: Dunhuang Sleeper Y667/668
properties.highlight: The branded “Dunhuang” sleeper leaves Lanzhou at 18:00 and follows the Hexi Corridor’s Great Wall forts overnight, arriving near the Mogao caves by dawn.

properties.name: Golmud–Korla Railway
properties.highlight: Opened 2020 across the Altun Shan between Qinghai and Xinjiang: 1,206 km of salt flats, desert and near-total emptiness. One of the loneliest overnight rides on Earth.

properties.name: Petit train d’Artouste
properties.highlight: Built for the dam works of the 1920s: 500 mm open cars creep along a cliff ledge at 1,940 m from the La Sagette gondola to Lac d’Artouste.

properties.name: Train à Vapeur des Cévennes
properties.highlight: Steam between Anduze and Saint-Jean-du-Gard: across the Gardon on four viaducts, past the giant bamboo of Prafrance. Forty open-window minutes in the Cévennes.

properties.name: Oran–Béchar Night Train
properties.highlight: Algeria’s Sahara sleeper, revived in December 2024: couchettes leave Oran at nightfall and reach Béchar at the Saoura’s edge by sunrise.

properties.name: Le Train Rouge
properties.highlight: France’s longest tourist railway: 60 km from Rivesaltes’ vineyards into the Fenouillèdes gorges beneath the Cathar castles of Quéribus and Puilaurens.

properties.name: Intercités de Nuit
properties.highlight: Asleep out of Austerlitz, awake on the Côte Vermeille: the sleeper threads Collioure, Port-Vendres and Banyuls to the last stop before Spain.

properties.name: Ligne de la Côte Bleue
properties.highlight: An everyday TER on a corniche of 23 tunnels and 18 viaducts: calanque after calanque between L’Estaque and Martigues for a few euros.

properties.name: Panoramique des Dômes
properties.highlight: A Strub rack railway spirals up the dormant Puy de Dôme volcano: 5.3 km and 500 vertical metres to the Roman Temple of Mercury at 1,406 m.

properties.name: Le Grand Tour
properties.highlight: Puy du Fou’s rolling theatre: a Belle Époque sleeper loops 4,000 km around France in six days, actors staging a mystery from Reims to Chenonceau.

properties.name: Intercités de Nuit
properties.highlight: The Aveyron sleeper: off the Limoges main line at Brive, then Rocamadour, the Lot valley and Rodez by breakfast, with Albi through-cars on weekends.

properties.name: Velay Express
properties.highlight: France’s highest steam railway: a 1906 Mallet hauls metre-gauge trains across the 1,000 m Velay plateau between Raucoules and Saint-Agrève.

properties.name: Chemin de fer de la Vendée
properties.operator: Chemin de Fer de la Vendée
properties.highlight: Belle-Époque dining on the move: restored CIWL Orient Express diners behind an 030 T steam engine, three viaducts between Mortagne and Les Herbiers.

properties.name: Train des Mouettes
properties.highlight: Steam at 30 km/h beside the Seudre oyster beds: an 1891 Schneider, France’s oldest working steam engine, still hauls the gulls’ train to La Tremblade.

properties.name: Train Thur Doller Alsace
properties.highlight: Sunday steam in the Doller valley: a century-old 030 T ambles from Cernay to Sentheim past storks, orchards and the first folds of the Vosges.

properties.name: Dia Tsara
properties.highlight: Madagascar’s east-coast revival of 2023: once a week, twelve hours from Moramanga through rainforest gorges to the Pangalanes shore and Toamasina.

properties.name: Tren Solar de la Quebrada
properties.operator: Tren Solar de la Quebrada S.E.
properties.highlight: Lithium-battery railcars charged by a solar farm glide through the UNESCO-listed Quebrada de Humahuaca to Tilcara: the first solar-powered train in the Americas.

properties.name: Media Distancia R-3f
properties.highlight: Three metre-gauge trains a day still thread all 119 km of the 1898 Santander–Bilbao railway, winding through green Basque and Cantabrian valleys.

properties.name: Ferrocarril de Riotinto
properties.train: Restored mine coaches; steam on winter Sundays
properties.highlight: Restored mining stock creeps along the blood-red Río Tinto through a Mars-like landscape mined for 5,000 years, and Victorian steam hauls it on winter Sundays.

properties.name: Maria Fumaça (VFCJ)
properties.highlight: Brazil’s flagship steam railway: ABPF volunteers fire century-old locomotives up the 1875 Mogiana trunk from Campinas to Jaguariúna every weekend.

properties.name: Caminho de Ferro de Moçâmedes
properties.train: CFM weekly express, restaurant & multimedia cars
properties.highlight: Angola’s third great trunk climbs from the desert port of Namibe over the Serra da Chela to Menongue: 756 rebuilt km, with a weekly express since December 2023.

properties.name: Tren Macho
properties.highlight: Peru’s beloved Tren Macho is back: free trains roll the first 57 km down the Mantaro valley to Cuenca while the century-old Huancavelica line is modernized.

properties.name: Bonde de Santa Teresa
properties.highlight: Latin America’s oldest electric tramway (1896) rattles across the Carioca Aqueduct’s arches and up Santa Teresa’s cobbled lanes high above downtown Rio.

properties.name: Tren de Felipe II
properties.highlight: An ALCO diesel and 1940s coaches staffed by costumed actors climb from Príncipe Pío into the Guadarrama foothills to Philip II’s colossal monastery-palace.

properties.name: Expresso Turístico
properties.highlight: A 1952 ALCO diesel and 1960s Budd cars leave Luz station on weekends for Paranapiacaba, the fog-wrapped English railway village at the rim of the Serra do Mar.

properties.name: Media Distancia R-1f
properties.highlight: Europe’s longest narrow-gauge ride: two trains a day take seven hours to weave around Galicia’s rias and along the Asturian cliffs from Ferrol to Oviedo.

properties.name: Treno Natura
properties.highlight: Steam excursions across the UNESCO Val d’Orcia: 51 km of cypress avenues, clay badlands and Brunello vineyards on an 1865 branch kept alive purely for the Treno Natura.

properties.name: Porrettana Express
properties.highlight: The 1864 Porrettana was Italy’s first railway across the Apennines: E.626-hauled Centoporte coaches now relive its 26 ‰ climb from Pistoia to the spa town of Porretta.

properties.name: Trenino Verde
properties.highlight: The Trenino Verde’s second living branch: 46 km of 950 mm track twisting off Macomer’s basalt plateau down to the palm-lined seafront at Bosa Marina.

properties.name: Irpinia Express
properties.highlight: Closed in 2010, revived for excursions: the 1895 Ofanto-valley line threads 119 km of viaducts, vineyards and hill villages from Avellino to lonely Rocchetta junction.

properties.name: Treno di Dante
properties.operator: Il Treno di Dante · Fondazione FS
properties.highlight: Vintage Centoporte coaches link Dante’s Florence with his tomb in Ravenna over the Apennine Faentina line, joined by new direct Sunday trains since July 2026.

properties.name: Ferrovia Trento–Malè–Mezzana
properties.highlight: A metre-gauge electric line out of Trento: through the Rocchetta gorge into apple-carpeted Val di Non and Val di Sole, ending at Mezzana beneath the Brenta Dolomites.

properties.name: Chemin de Fer à Vapeur des Trois Vallées
properties.highlight: Steam on the 1854 Entre-Sambre-et-Meuse line: CFV3V engines bark up the wooded Viroin valley to the great museum shed at Treignes.

properties.name: Lennakatten
properties.highlight: Steam from the edge of a university city: the 891 mm Lennakatten rolls 33 km through Uppland forests and lakeside summer halts to the engine sheds at Faringe.

properties.name: Krøderbanen
properties.highlight: Norway’s longest museum railway: 26 km of the 1872 Krøder line preserved whole, with stations, water cranes and NSB steam between Vikersund and the lake at Krøderen.

properties.name: Gamle Vossebanen
properties.highlight: The 1883 Voss line’s surviving loop outside Bergen: NSB 18c steam between Garnes and Midttun, bypassed by new tunnels in 1964 and kept alive by volunteers.

properties.name: Thamshavnbanen
properties.highlight: Built in 1908 for Orkla’s copper ore: the oldest alternating-current railway still in service, running its original 6.6 kV motor coaches along the green Orkla valley.

properties.name: Setesdalsbanen
properties.highlight: Norway’s oldest museum railway, volunteer-run since 1964: 1890s narrow-gauge steam puffing up the Otra river from Grovane to the little terminus at Røyknes.

properties.name: Veluwsche Stoomtrein
properties.highlight: The Netherlands’ biggest steam operation: wartime German Kriegsloks and a forty-strong fleet work the 1887 Veluwe country line between Apeldoorn and Dieren.

properties.name: Mariager–Handest Veteranjernbane
properties.highlight: Denmark’s leading veteran railway: 1909 Henschel steam from the fjord port of Mariager over rolling moraine hills to Handest, run in 1950s private-railway style.

properties.name: TOHOKU EMOTION
properties.highlight: A restaurant on rails (open kitchen car, chef’s courses at every seat) rolling the Sanriku surf from Hachinohe to Kuji along the Tanesashi coast.

properties.name: Tama Densha
properties.highlight: Eiji Mitooka’s white train painted with 101 cartoon Tamas trundles to Kishi, where calico stationmaster Tama famously saved the line; a cat shrine now guards the platform.

properties.name: SL Banetsu Monogatari
properties.highlight: C57 180, “the Lady”, hauls seven retro coaches up the Agano river gorge from Niitsu to castle-town Aizu-Wakamatsu, one of Japan’s last full-size mainline steam runs.

properties.name: Setsugekka
properties.highlight: Crimson-and-silver resort train with Japan’s largest train windows, serving regional courses on a slow sweep from Mt Myoko’s snow country to the Sea of Japan at Itoigawa.

properties.name: Iyonada Monogatari
properties.highlight: A retro maroon-and-gold diner idling along the Iyonada shore: brunch above the waves and a pause at Shimonada, Japan’s most photographed seaside platform.

properties.name: Kairi
properties.highlight: Kairi means “sea and village”: a hybrid diner serving Niigata and Shonai delicacies while threading the Sasagawa-nagare, 11 km of wave-gnawed rocks on the Uetsu coast.

properties.name: GRAN Tenku
properties.highlight: Nankai’s deep-red 2026 flagship runs through from Namba’s neon to Gokurakubashi, grinding up 50‰ cedar slopes to the cable car for sacred Koyasan, with a lounge and bar aboard.

properties.name: Umisachi-Yamasachi
properties.highlight: Obi-cedar railcars named for the sea-luck, mountain-luck myth skim the Nichinan palm coast past Aoshima’s Devil’s Washboard reefs to the fishing port of Nango.

properties.name: A-Train (Amakusa)
properties.highlight: A jazz-soundtracked bar on rails (dark wood, stained glass, “A-Highball” in hand) swinging along the Ariake tidal flats from Kumamoto to the Amakusa ferry at Misumi.

properties.name: HIGH RAIL 1375
properties.highlight: Grinds to 1,375 m at JR’s highest rail point below Yatsugatake: observatory seats by day, a stargazing dome and astronomer-guided night runs under the Milky Way.

properties.name: etSETOra
properties.highlight: etSETOra drifts the Kure Line’s island-studded Seto shore with Hiroshima patissiers’ sweets courses and a sake bar. Since 2025 it runs clear through to Fukuyama.

properties.name: SL Paleo Express
properties.highlight: The closest steam to Tokyo: wartime C58 363 huffs four retro coaches from Kumagaya into the Chichibu hills past Nagatoro’s rock terraces, running since 1988.

properties.name: Koshino Shu*Kura
properties.highlight: A sake brewery on wheels (Niigata tasting bar, live jazz, a long pause on the sea cliff at Aoumigawa) winding via Nagaoka into snow-country Tokamachi.

properties.name: Belles montagnes et mer
properties.highlight: “Beautiful mountains and sea”: an emerald art-gallery railcar where a sushi chef works the counter as Amaharashi bay frames 3,000-metre Tateyama across the water.

properties.name: Blue Symphony
properties.highlight: Navy-and-gold Blue Symphony glides from Osaka Abenobashi to holy Yoshino, the UNESCO cherry mountain, with a lounge bar, cake sets and armchairs in a reborn commuter train.

properties.name: Tosa Toki no Yoake no Monogatari
properties.highlight: Ryoma-themed “dawn of a new era” train pairs Tosa seafood with Pacific panoramas above Susaki and Tosa-Kure bays, locals waving it through tea fields to Kubokawa.

properties.name: Hanayome Noren
properties.highlight: A rolling Kaga bridal curtain: vermilion-and-black cars finished in Wajima-lacquer motifs and gold leaf, serving Ishikawa sweets en route to Wakura Onsen’s seaside baths.

properties.name: Rokumon
properties.highlight: Rokumon wears the Sanada clan’s six-coin crest in deep crimson, serving kaiseki under Mt Asama on the old Shinetsu main line from Karuizawa down to Zenko-ji’s Nagano.

properties.name: Ametsuchi
properties.highlight: Lapis-blue Ametsuchi (“heaven and earth”, from the Kojiki’s opening line) roams the San’in coast’s breakers past Mt Daisen and Lake Shinji from Tottori to Izumo.

properties.name: Ruskeala Express
properties.highlight: Russia’s only daily steam service: blue retro cars behind a vintage locomotive from Sortavala to Ruskeala’s flooded marble canyon, staged down to conductors in 1900s dress.

properties.name: Night Express
properties.highlight: Ukraine’s overnight hop across the Carpathians: asleep through Lviv, awake for the climb past Skole into the 2018 twin-bore Beskyd tunnel, then down the valley to Uzhhorod.

properties.name: Hutsulshchyna
properties.highlight: Ukraine’s flagship sleeper into Hutsul country: dusk in Kyiv, dawn above the Prut gorge at Yaremche, then Vorokhta’s stone viaduct and the Yablunytsia pass down to Rakhiv.

properties.name: Labytnangi
properties.highlight: Fifty-two hours north to the last station on the Gulag-built Dead Road: the Chum–Labytnangi branch opened in 1948 and stops on the Ob, across the water from Salekhard.

properties.name: Vorkuta
properties.highlight: Two nights up the Stalin-era Pechora mainline to Vorkuta, a coal city beyond the Arctic Circle that no all-year road reaches; train № 41 is its lifeline to Moscow.

properties.name: Premium
properties.highlight: The southern flagship since 1964 (first Ritsa, then Sochi, Premium since 2009): 1,761 km from Kazansky station to the subtropical Black Sea platforms of Adler in 23 hours.

properties.name: Yantar
properties.highlight: Running since 1964, the Yantar threads Moscow to Russia’s Baltic exclave via Minsk and Vilnius, the last corridor where Russian passenger trains still cross the EU.

properties.name: Sakhalin Night Train
properties.highlight: Russia’s island sleeper: 613 km up Sakhalin’s east coast to oil-town Nogliki, on a railway begun under Japanese rule that kept its narrow gauge until regauging in 2019.

properties.name: AYaM Yakutia Train
properties.highlight: 23 hours north from the BAM at Tynda across permafrost to Nizhny Bestyakh on the Lena, one river crossing short of Yakutsk. Russia’s newest long-distance railway.

properties.name: Zhemchuzhina Kavkaza
properties.highlight: A hotel on rails looping from Moscow around the North Caucasus (Maykop, Kislovodsk, Vladikavkaz, Grozny, seaside Derbent and Nalchik): seven days, one ticket, since 2021.

properties.name: Stoosbahn
properties.highlight: The world’s steepest funicular: a 110% maximum gradient climbed by barrel cabins that rotate to keep the floor level, 744 m up to car-free Stoos.

properties.name: Niesenbahn
properties.train: Two-section funicular; car change at Schwandegg
properties.highlight: Climbs 1,643 m over 3.5 km up the pyramid of the Niesen, and the service stairway alongside is the longest on earth at 11,674 steps.

properties.name: Gelmerbahn
properties.train: Open-air 24-seat cars of 1926, public rides since 2001
properties.highlight: An open-car ride up a 106% grade, Europe’s steepest funicular until Stoos overtook it in 2017, built to serve the Gelmersee dam works.

properties.name: Funiculaire Sierre–Crans-Montana
properties.train: Fully renewed cars, track and drive (2022)
properties.highlight: Switzerland’s longest funicular: 4.2 km and 927 m of climb from the Rhône valley vineyards at Sierre to the Crans-Montana plateau.

properties.name: Fribourg Funicular
properties.train: 1899 cars hauled by 3,000-litre wastewater ballast tanks
properties.highlight: Europe’s last funicular driven by wastewater: since 1899 the descending car is weighted with up to 3,000 litres of city sewage.

properties.name: Hungerburgbahn
properties.train: Tilting-floor hybrid funicular cabins; Zaha Hadid stations
properties.highlight: A 2007 hybrid funicular with Zaha Hadid’s sculpted glass stations. Its cabins tilt to stay level from the flat river crossing to a 46% climb.

properties.name: FestungsBahn Salzburg
properties.train: Panoramic glass cars from the 2011 renewal
properties.highlight: Austria’s oldest funicular in service (1892) rises into Hohensalzburg, one of Europe’s largest intact medieval fortresses, in 54 seconds.

properties.name: Mendelbahn
properties.train: Two counterbalanced cars with passing loop
properties.highlight: Europe’s longest and steepest funicular at its 1903 opening, still climbing 854 m at up to 64% from South Tyrol’s wine country to the Mendel Pass.

properties.name: Como–Brunate Funicular
properties.train: Two counterbalanced cars with mid-line passing loop
properties.highlight: Since 1894 the link between Como’s lakefront and hilltop Brunate, ’the balcony of the Alps’, climbing at up to 55% above Lake Como.

properties.name: Funicolare Centrale
properties.train: Two four-car trains, about 450 passengers each
properties.highlight: One of the world’s busiest funiculars: around 10 million passengers a year between Via Toledo and the Vomero hill.

properties.name: Capri Funicular
properties.train: Two counterbalanced trains between port and Piazzetta
properties.highlight: Capri’s main street since 1907: hoists ferry arrivals from Marina Grande harbour 138 m up to the island’s famous Piazzetta in four minutes.

properties.name: Montmartre Funicular
properties.highlight: Paris’s shortcut to Sacré-Cœur since 1900: 108 m of track, 36 m of rise and about two million riders a year.

properties.name: Fourvière Funicular (la ficelle)
properties.highlight: Lyon ran the world’s first urban funiculars from 1862; today’s F2 of 1900 lifts riders from UNESCO-listed Vieux Lyon to the Fourvière basilica.

properties.name: Tibidabo Funicular (Cuca de Llum)
properties.train: Glass-roofed ’Cuca de Llum’ trains from the 2021 rebuild
properties.highlight: Barcelona’s 1901 summit line to the Tibidabo amusement park and Sagrat Cor temple, reborn in 2021 as the glass ’glow-worm’ trains.

properties.name: Montjuïc Funicular
properties.train: Twin three-car trains from the 1992 Olympic rebuild
properties.highlight: Metro-integrated since 1928 and rebuilt for the 1992 Olympics, and among Europe’s highest-capacity funiculars at 8,000 passengers an hour.

properties.name: Bom Jesus do Monte Funicular
properties.operator: Irmandade do Bom Jesus do Monte
properties.highlight: The world’s oldest water-balance funicular in continuous service (1882), climbing beside the baroque stairway of UNESCO-listed Bom Jesus do Monte.

properties.name: Budavári Sikló
properties.train: Replica 19th-century wooden cars Margit and Gellért (1986)
properties.highlight: Opened 1870 as Europe’s second funicular; destroyed in WWII and rebuilt in 1986, it climbs to Buda Castle inside the UNESCO Danube panorama.

properties.name: Zagreb Funicular (Uspinjača)
properties.highlight: At 66 m one of the world’s shortest public funiculars, linking Zagreb’s Lower and Upper Towns since 1890.

properties.name: Ljubljana Castle Funicular
properties.train: Single glass panoramic cabin with counterweight (2006)
properties.highlight: A glass funicular of 2006 rising 70 m in one minute from the old-town market square to Ljubljana Castle, the capital’s defining landmark.

properties.name: Fløibanen
properties.highlight: Norway’s best-known funicular (1918): 844 m and ~300 m of rise from central Bergen to the Fløyen viewpoint above the fjord city.

properties.name: Lynton & Lynmouth Cliff Railway
properties.train: Original 1890 twin cars, each with a 700-gallon water tank
properties.highlight: The world’s highest and steepest fully water-powered railway (1890): gravity and 700-gallon tanks alone work its twin cars on a 58% grade.

properties.name: Nerobergbahn
properties.train: Historic 1888 cars driven by 7,000-litre water ballast tanks
properties.highlight: Germany’s only surviving water-ballast funicular (1888), still climbing Wiesbaden’s Neroberg on 7,000 litres of tank water and no engine.

properties.name: Kyiv Funicular
properties.highlight: Kyiv’s 1905 funicular climbs a 36% grade from riverside Podil to the St Michael’s monastery quarter, with 2.8 million riders a year even in wartime.

properties.name: Tbilisi Funicular
properties.train: Doppelmayr Garaventa cars from the 2012 reconstruction
properties.highlight: Tbilisi’s 1905 funicular to Mtatsminda, the city’s highest viewpoint. Derelict after 2000, rebuilt by Doppelmayr Garaventa and reopened 2012.

properties.name: Tünel
properties.train: Two rubber-tyred cars from the 1971 electrification
properties.highlight: Opened 1875: the world’s second-oldest underground urban railway after London’s, and the oldest underground funicular still running.

properties.name: F1 Taksim–Kabataş Funicular
properties.highlight: A deep-bored 2006 funicular linking Bosphorus ferries and trams at Kabataş with Taksim Square: Istanbul’s modern echo of the 1875 Tünel.

properties.name: Monongahela Incline
properties.highlight: Opened 1870, the oldest continuously operating funicular in the United States, and still a fare-integrated everyday transit link up Mount Washington.

properties.name: Duquesne Incline
properties.train: Original 1877 J.G. Brill wooden cars in cherry and oak
properties.operator: Society for the Preservation of the Duquesne Heights Incline
properties.highlight: Original 1877 wooden Brill cars still climb the 30-degree grade to Grandview Avenue and Pittsburgh’s postcard skyline overlook.

properties.name: Lookout Mountain Incline Railway
properties.train: Two counterbalanced cars with midway passing loop
properties.highlight: ’America’s Most Amazing Mile’ since 1895: the 72.7% grade near the summit ranks among the steepest on any passenger railway.

properties.name: Angels Flight
properties.train: Twin 1901 cars Olivet and Sinai, restored 2017
properties.highlight: Billed the world’s shortest incorporated railway since 1901, the 91 m Bunker Hill hop costs $1.50 and starred in film noir and La La Land.

properties.name: Fenelon Place Elevator
properties.train: Two counterbalanced house-shaped cars, winched at 41 degrees
properties.highlight: Built in 1882 so banker J.K. Graves could ride the bluff home for lunch, and billed as the world’s shortest, steepest scenic railway.

properties.name: Old Quebec Funicular
properties.train: Two independent panoramic cabins from the 1998 rebuild
properties.highlight: Scaling Cap Diamant at 45 degrees since 1879, it links Petit-Champlain’s boutiques to Dufferin Terrace beside the Château Frontenac.

properties.name: Falls Incline Railway
properties.train: Two enclosed 40-passenger cabins from the 2013 rebuild
properties.highlight: Niagara Parks bills it the world’s slowest funicular: a 62-second, 3.5 km/h glide linking Fallsview’s hotels to Horseshoe Falls at Table Rock.

properties.name: Funicular de Santiago
properties.train: Two 1925 counterbalanced cars, rebuilt 2020–22, zoo mid-station
properties.highlight: A 1925 funicular and national monument rising to Santiago’s hilltop Virgin. Pope John Paul II rode it during his 1987 visit.

properties.name: Ascensor Concepción
properties.train: Two seven-passenger cars at 46 degrees, once water-balance powered
properties.highlight: Valparaíso’s oldest ascensor (1883) began on water ballast and still hoists riders 69 m from the Turri clock up to Paseo Gervasoni.

properties.name: Monserrate Funicular
properties.train: Two counterbalanced trains of up to 80 passengers
properties.highlight: Hauling pilgrims since 1929 up 460 vertical metres to Bogotá’s 3,152 m summit sanctuary, one of the world’s highest funicular rides.

properties.name: Plano Inclinado Gonçalves
properties.train: Two 36-passenger cabins, re-equipped in the 2025 requalification
properties.highlight: Built in 1874 with Esslingen machinery, Salvador’s cliff-face inclined plane still links the Comércio to UNESCO-listed Pelourinho, free of charge.

properties.name: Flying Dutchman Funicular
properties.train: Two 40-seat cars named after ships wrecked off the Cape
properties.highlight: Africa’s only commercial funicular, named for the ghost ship said to haunt Cape Point, lifts visitors 87 m toward the 1859 lighthouse.

properties.name: Peak Tram
properties.highlight: Asia’s first funicular (1888), climbing almost 400 m over the Victoria Harbour skyline, with four million riders a year on 6th-generation cars.

properties.name: Penang Hill Railway
properties.highlight: Malaysia’s only funicular since 1923: the Swiss-rebuilt line climbs 691 m through what was once the steepest funicular tunnel in the world.

properties.name: Carmelit
properties.train: Two stepped Von Roll/Doppelmayr trains, refurbished 2018
properties.highlight: Israel’s only fully underground railway and one of the world’s smallest metros: six stepped stations rising 274 m inside Mount Carmel.

properties.name: Koyasan Cable Car
properties.highlight: Nankai’s 1930 cable car hoists pilgrims up the final 328 m to UNESCO-listed Kōyasan, the mountaintop monastery town of Shingon Buddhism.

properties.name: Hakone Tozan Cable Car
properties.highlight: Japan’s second-oldest funicular (1921) links Gōra with the Hakone Ropeway at Sōunzan: the cable-hauled leg of the classic Hakone circuit.

properties.name: Mount Takao Cable Car
properties.highlight: Japan’s steepest railway (a 608 permil grade near the top), lifting hikers up Michelin three-star Mount Takao since 1927.

properties.name: Ikoma Cable Car
properties.highlight: Japan’s first cable railway (1918) still climbs Mount Ikoma as the country’s only double-track funicular, famed for its animal-faced cars.

properties.name: Sakamoto Cable
properties.highlight: Japan’s longest funicular, 2,025 m up Mount Hiei to UNESCO-listed Enryaku-ji with Lake Biwa views, running since 1927.

properties.name: Katoomba Scenic Railway
properties.train: 84-seat glass-roofed carriages (2013) with adjustable seat recline
properties.highlight: The Guinness-listed steepest passenger railway on earth: a 52-degree plunge into the Jamison Valley on an 1880s coal-mine incline.

properties.name: Wellington Cable Car
properties.highlight: Wellington’s red icon since 1902, climbing 120 m from Lambton Quay to the Kelburn lookout. Rebuilt as a true funicular in 1979.

properties.name: Southeastern Highspeed
properties.highlight: Britain’s only domestic high-speed service: 225 km/h down HS1 to Ashford, then the 1844 South Eastern main line past Folkestone and under the white cliffs into Dover.

properties.name: Southeastern Highspeed
properties.highlight: The Javelin put Margate 86 minutes from London: HS1 at 225 km/h as far as Ashford, then the 1846 Canterbury line across east Kent to the Thanet coast.

properties.name: Toulouse–Bayonne railway
properties.highlight: Runs the whole width of the south-west along the foothills of the Pyrenees, opened in stages between 1861 and 1867 and still the direct way from the Atlantic to Toulouse.

properties.name: Stralsund–Berlin railway
properties.highlight: One of the oldest railways in Western Pomerania, built from 1863 by the Berlin-Stettin company and now the fast run down from Stralsund to Berlin.

properties.name: Mälaren Line
properties.highlight: Follows the northern shore of Lake Mälaren from Stockholm through Västerås to Örebro, double track most of the way and rebuilt for high-speed running in 2005.

properties.name: Rome–Ancona railway
properties.highlight: Crosses the Apennines sea to sea, from the Adriatic at Ancona through Foligno, Spoleto and Terni to Orte on the Rome main line.

properties.name: Coutras–Tulle line
properties.highlight: Single track, never electrified, opened piece by piece from 1857: the cross-country link between the Paris–Bordeaux and Orléans–Montauban main lines.

properties.name: Haparanda Line
properties.highlight: Sweden's only railway to the Finnish border, and freight-only from 1992 until passengers came back in 2021.

properties.name: Danube Valley Railway
properties.highlight: Threads the young Danube from Ulm through Blaubeuren and Riedlingen to Sigmaringen, single-tracked and largely unelectrified, and once part of the Munich–Freiburg main line.

properties.name: Treuchtlingen–Würzburg railway
properties.highlight: Opened in three sections from 1859 and one of Germany's oldest main lines, running through Franconia via Ansbach and Ochsenfurt into Würzburg.

properties.name: Ruse–Kaspichan railway
properties.highlight: The first railway ever built in Bulgaria, opened on 7 November 1866 from the Danube quays at Ruse toward the Black Sea, and still line 9 of the national network.

properties.name: Blekinge Coast Line
properties.highlight: The coast line through Skåne and Blekinge, opened in 1898 and now the Öresundståg run east to the naval city of Karlskrona.

properties.name: Skåne Line
properties.highlight: Skånebanan links eastern and western Skåne by way of Hässleholm: an 1865 railway that only got its collective name from Banverket in 1990.

properties.name: Stendal–Uelzen railway
properties.highlight: Mostly single track yet electrified and main-line rated, crossing the Altmark from Stendal to Uelzen with Salzwedel the one town of any size on the way.

properties.name: Craiova–Calafat railway
