properties.highlight: A secondary single line down to the Danube, largely unelectrified, that found new purpose when the Calafat–Vidin bridge opened the way into Bulgaria.

properties.name: Bari–Taranto railway
properties.highlight: 104 km across the Murge plateau from Bari through Gioia del Colle to Taranto, now covered end to end by Frecciarossa in a little over an hour.

properties.name: Pyhrn railway
properties.highlight: Climbs from Linz over the Pyhrn Pass to Selzthal, tying the Westbahn to the Enns valley through the northern limestone Alps.

properties.name: Brescia–Iseo–Edolo railway
properties.highlight: Runs the length of Lake Iseo and up the Valcamonica to Edolo under the Adamello: standard gauge, single track, unelectrified, built in stages from 1885.

properties.name: Langå–Struer railway
properties.highlight: Central Jutland end to end: single track opened section by section from 1863, Langå to Viborg to Skive to the fjord port at Struer.

properties.name: Bratislava–Komárno railway
properties.highlight: Follows the Danube across the Žitný ostrov plain, and in 2012 became the first Slovak line handed over to a private operator.

properties.name: Libourne–Le Buisson line
properties.highlight: 97 km of single track east from the Paris–Bordeaux main line into the Périgord, opened in 1869 and still the cross-country link toward Agen and Cahors.

properties.name: Zvolen–Vrútky railway
properties.highlight: Slovak line 170 through the mountains north of Zvolen: the Banská Bystrica–Dolná Štubňa section alone, built 1936–40, has 22 tunnels totalling 12.2 km.

properties.name: Košice–Prešov railway
properties.highlight: Slovakia’s second city reached from its first: the Kaschau–Oderberg company opened the branch on 1 September 1870, north up the Hornád and off the Bohumín main line at Kysak.

properties.name: Livorno–Florence railway
properties.highlight: The Ferrovia Leopolda of the 1840s, still carrying Tuscany's busiest regional run from Livorno and Pisa through Pontedera and Empoli into Florence.

properties.name: Margecany–Červená Skala railway
properties.highlight: Single track through the Slovak Ore Mountains and along the south-east flank of the Low Tatras, climbing to the spiral and viaduct at Telgárt.

properties.name: Main-Neckar Railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1846 down the Upper Rhine plain west of the Odenwald, one of Germany's oldest railways and still the local road from Frankfurt through Darmstadt and Bensheim to Heidelberg.

properties.name: Łódź–Kutno railway
properties.highlight: Łódź's link north to the Warsaw–Poznań main line at Kutno, through Zgierz, Ozorków and Łęczyca, part of it doubling as the city's freight ring.

properties.name: Saar Railway
properties.highlight: The Saarstrecke of 1858–60 follows the Saar from Trier up to Saarbrücken, one of the oldest railways in Germany and still the valley's stopping service.

properties.name: Rennes–Saint-Malo railway
properties.highlight: Brittany's run to the sea: 81 km from Rennes to the walled port of Saint-Malo, opened in 1864 and now covered non-stop in three quarters of an hour.

properties.name: Valence–Moirans railway
properties.highlight: Built by the PLM and opened on 9 May 1864 to join Valence to Grenoble, double track over two thirds of its length and electrified in the 2010s.

properties.name: Regensburg–Ingolstadt railway
properties.highlight: Single track but electrified up the Danube valley from Regensburg to Ingolstadt. With the Ingolstadt–Neuoffingen line, it forms the Bavarian Donautalbahn.

properties.name: Stralsund–Rostock railway
properties.highlight: Joins the two Hanseatic cities of the Baltic coast: single track, electrified, and rebuilt as German Unity transport project no. 1.

properties.name: Rennes–Redon railway
properties.highlight: The 1862 line down the Vilaine from Rennes to Redon, the shared first leg of Brittany's runs to Nantes and to Quimper.

properties.name: Augsburg–Nördlingen railway
properties.highlight: Part of the Ludwig South-North Railway of 1844: fast electrified track from Augsburg to Donauwörth, then the branch on to the walled crater town of Nördlingen.

properties.name: Ystad Line
properties.highlight: Malmö to the ferry town of Ystad across southern Scania, where the Österlen Line carries on to Simrishamn.

properties.name: Vorarlbergbahn
properties.highlight: Vorarlberg end to end: from Lindau on Lake Constance up the Rhine valley and the Walgau to Bludenz, where the Arlberg and Montafon lines begin.

properties.name: Miskolc–Bánréve–Ózd railway
properties.highlight: Branches off the Hatvan–Miskolc main line and runs up the Sajó through Bánréve to the steel town of Ózd, on the Slovak border.

properties.name: Grenoble–Montmélian railway
properties.highlight: Built double-track by the PLM and opened on 15 September 1864 to join Grenoble to the Savoy main line; fully electrified only in December 2013.

properties.name: Zemitāni–Skulte railway
properties.highlight: Latvian 1,520 mm track north from Riga to the Gulf coast at Skulte: what remains in service of the old Riga–Rūjiena and Riga–Tallinn route, cut at the Estonian border in 1992.

properties.name: Neuchâtel–Pontarlier railway
properties.highlight: The Franco-Suisse line of 1860 through the Val-de-Travers, single track over the Jura from Pontarlier down to the Neuchâtel lakeshore.

properties.name: Lollandsbanen
properties.highlight: Opened in 1874 and still crossing Lolland from Nykøbing Falster through Maribo to the shipyard town of Nakskov.

properties.name: Prättigau Line
properties.highlight: Metre-gauge Rhaetian track climbing the Prättigau from the Rhine valley at Landquart to the high spa town of Davos, open since 1890.

properties.name: Engadine Line
properties.highlight: Metre gauge down the Lower Engadine from the Albula line at Bever to the spa at Scuol-Tarasp, opened in 1913 and never joined to Austria.

properties.name: Tallinn–Paldiski railway
properties.highlight: Estonia's oldest railway west from Tallinn, opened in 1870 to the ice-free naval harbour at Paldiski on the Baltic.

properties.name: Seetalbahn
properties.highlight: Opened in 1883 by British investors down the Seetal lakes to Lucerne. For a century a roadside light railway, it was rebuilt on its own alignment in the 2000s.

properties.name: Kystbanen
properties.highlight: The Sound coast line of 1897, one of Denmark's busiest: Copenhagen out past the Øresund beaches to Elsinore and Kronborg.

properties.name: Biel–La Chaux-de-Fonds railway
properties.highlight: Single track up out of Biel through the Jura gorges to the watchmaking city of La Chaux-de-Fonds at 1,000 m, worked since 1874.

properties.name: Frederiksværk Line
properties.highlight: North Zealand branch line: Hillerød to Frederiksværk from 1897, on to the Kattegat ferry harbour at Hundested from 1916.

properties.name: Arendal Line
properties.highlight: The surviving southern stub of a line that once ran 90 km inland: electrified feeder trains down from the Sørland main line at Nelaug to the coast at Arendal.

properties.name: Figeac–Arvant railway
properties.highlight: 170 km of single unelectrified track across the Massif Central, tying the Brive–Toulouse main line to the Cévennes line at Arvant.

properties.name: Székesfehérvár–Szombathely railway
properties.highlight: Electrified but mostly single track, crossing western Hungary from Szombathely through the Bakony foothills to Székesfehérvár.

properties.name: Tampere–Pori railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1895 and following the Kokemäenjoki river down to the Gulf of Bothnia, with only five intermediate stations in 132 km.

properties.name: Vejle–Holstebro railway
properties.highlight: Single track right across Jutland, built in pieces between 1894 and 1914 from the Vejle fjord to Herning and the west.

properties.name: Debrecen–Füzesabony railway
properties.highlight: Single track and unelectrified across the Great Plain, crossing the Tisza and the shallows of Lake Tisza at Tiszafüred.

properties.name: Győr–Sopron railway
properties.highlight: Opened on 2 January 1876 by the Raab-Oedenburg-Ebenfurth company, and still run by its successor GYSEV rather than by MÁV.

properties.name: Jyväskylä–Pieksämäki railway
properties.highlight: Finnish 1,524 mm track through the lake country, one stop in 79 km between the junction town of Pieksämäki and Jyväskylä.

properties.name: Győr–Veszprém railway
properties.highlight: The Bakonyvasút: a slow single track that leaves the Győr–Szentgotthárd line and climbs through the wooded Bakony hills to Veszprém.

properties.name: Jura Railway
properties.highlight: The Jurabahn of 1857 follows the Birs out of Basel into the French-speaking Jura, through Delémont and the Moutier gorges down to Biel.

properties.name: Győr–Celldömölk railway
properties.highlight: MÁV line 10, single track and still unelectrified, running south-west from Győr across the Kisalföld plain to the junction at Celldömölk.

properties.name: Vercelli–Pavia railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1882–83 across the rice paddies between Piedmont and Lombardy, linking Vercelli to Pavia and the Po.

properties.name: Aachen–Mönchengladbach railway
properties.highlight: Built by the Aachen-Düsseldorf-Ruhrort company between 1852 and 1854: one of Germany's oldest lines, and still the freight road from the Ruhr to Belgium.

properties.name: Dombóvár–Bátaszék-line
properties.highlight: The Danube–Drava branch through southern Transdanubia, single track between the junctions at Dombóvár and Bátaszék.

properties.name: Thur Valley Line
properties.highlight: Switzerland's fourth-oldest railway, opened on 16 May 1855 down the Thur valley to Romanshorn, where trains once met the Lake Constance ferries.

properties.name: Olten–Lucerne railway
properties.highlight: Built by the Schweizerische Centralbahn and open to Lucerne since 1856: double track, electrified, and still the fast way north to Olten and Basel.

properties.name: Szombathely–Szentgotthárd railway
properties.highlight: The old Hungarian Western Railway toward Graz, now the through run from Szombathely to Szentgotthárd on the Austrian border.

properties.name: Tølløse Line
properties.highlight: A rural single track across western Zealand, joining the Northwest Line at Tølløse to the Copenhagen–Fredericia main line at Slagelse.

properties.name: Miskolc–Tornanádaska railway
properties.highlight: Hungarian line 94, a slow branch north of Miskolc up the Bódva valley to the Slovak border at Tornanádaska.

properties.name: Kiskunhalas–Kiskunfélegyháza railway
properties.highlight: Line 155 across the sandy Kiskunság between two market towns of the Great Plain, opened in 1912.

properties.name: Bern–Neuchâtel railway
properties.highlight: The Direkt Linie of 1901, driven almost dead straight across the Grand Marais, and still part of the shortest rail route from Bern to Paris.

properties.name: Burgdorf–Thun railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1899 as the first electrified main-line railway in Europe, running from Burgdorf over Konolfingen to Thun.

properties.name: Delémont–Delle railway
properties.highlight: Opened in stages from 1872 through the Jura canton (Glovelier, Porrentruy, Boncourt) and over the French border to Delle.

properties.name: Vestbanen
properties.highlight: Nebelgrisen, the 'Nebel pig': 37 km of unelectrified West Jutland branch line from Varde out to the dune coast at Nørre Nebel.

properties.name: Fribourg–Ins railway
properties.highlight: Single track built by the Fribourg–Morat–Anet company, running from Fribourg past Murten and its lake to Ins in the Seeland.

properties.name: Cadenazzo–Luino railway
properties.highlight: Hugs the north-eastern shore of Lake Maggiore, crossing from Ticino into Italy on the way to Luino.

properties.name: Tonkin Line
properties.highlight: Opened in 1859 by the Ligne d'Italie, running from the Rhône at Saint-Maurice out to Lake Geneva at Le Bouveret and the French border.

properties.name: Glarus Line
properties.highlight: The Glarnerlinie of 1859, single track up the Linth valley under the Glärnisch and the Tödi to the road-head at Linthal.

properties.name: Ciudad Real–Badajoz railway
properties.highlight: 338 km west across La Mancha and the Extremadura dehesa, from Ciudad Real to the Portuguese border city of Badajoz, on track opened in 1866.

properties.name: Linares Baeza–Almería railway
properties.highlight: Iberian gauge from the Alcázar–Cádiz main line at Linares down through the Sierra to the Mediterranean at Almería, through the desert country the spaghetti Westerns made famous.

properties.name: Pieksämäki–Joensuu railway
properties.highlight: Single track, unelectrified, running east through the Finnish lakes from the junction at Pieksämäki to Joensuu near the Russian border.

properties.name: Joensuu–Nurmes railway
properties.highlight: Dm12 railbuses up the shore of Lake Pielinen: the rails carry on to Kontiomäki, but passenger trains have stopped at Nurmes since 1993.

properties.name: Oulu–Kontiomäki railway
properties.highlight: 166 km of single electrified track inland from Oulu on the Gulf of Bothnia to Kontiomäki, where five railways meet.

properties.name: Wrocław–Poznań railway
properties.highlight: Silesia to Wielkopolska via Leszno, opened in 1856 and now part of TEN-T corridor E59 from Scandinavia south to Vienna and Budapest.

properties.name: Niversac–Agen railway
properties.highlight: A slow country line opened in 1863: three and a half hours for 164 km from the Garonne at Agen up through the Périgord to the Périgueux junction at Niversac.

properties.name: Iisalmi–Ylivieska railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1923 as the cross-country link between Finland's Savonia and Ostrobothnia main lines, 154 km through the forests of Kainuu.

properties.name: Castejón–Alsasua railway
properties.highlight: Iberian-gauge track up the Ebro and over into Navarre, opened in 1865 and still the Madrid–Basque Country road through Altsasu.

properties.name: Palatine Ludwig Railway
properties.highlight: The Pfälzische Ludwigsbahn of 1847, the Palatinate's main artery through Neustadt, Kaiserslautern and Homburg, and today part of the Paris–Frankfurt run.

properties.name: Turku–Toijala railway
properties.highlight: Finnish 1,524 mm gauge across Southwest Finland and Häme, joining the port of Turku to the Helsinki–Tampere main line at Toijala since 1876.

properties.name: Montluçon–Saint-Sulpice-Laurières line
properties.highlight: An 1864 cross-country line over the western edge of the Massif Central, from the Paris–Toulouse main line at Saint-Sulpice-Laurière to Montluçon.

properties.name: Haapamäki–Seinäjoki railway
properties.highlight: The middle section of the old Tampere–Vaasa railway of 1882, still carrying the diesel run west from the junction at Haapamäki.

properties.name: Munich–Simbach railway
properties.highlight: Opened on 1 May 1871 east from Munich through Markt Schwaben and Dorfen to Mühldorf and the Inn at Simbach: one of Germany's identified capacity bottlenecks.

properties.name: Mouchard–Bourg-en-Bresse railway
properties.highlight: Part of the Mulhouse–Besançon–Lyon route: a demanding northern section of climbs and falls through the Jura before it runs out onto the Bresse plain.

properties.name: Tampere–Haapamäki railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1902 north from Tampere into the lake and forest country of central Finland, meeting the Vaasa and Jyväskylä lines at Haapamäki.

properties.name: Iisalmi–Kontiomäki railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1904 through the forests of Kainuu, the northern half of the Savonia route from Iisalmi up to the five-way junction at Kontiomäki.

properties.name: Szombathely–Nagykanizsa railway
properties.highlight: Western Hungary north to south since 1865, from the Croatian-border junction at Nagykanizsa up past Zalaegerszeg to Szombathely.

properties.name: Limoges–Périgueux railway
properties.highlight: An 1861 line across the Limousin plateau, one stop in 99 km between the porcelain city of Limoges and Périgueux in the Dordogne.

properties.name: Krustpils–Rēzekne railway
properties.highlight: Latvian 1,524 mm track through Latgale, built as part of the Ventspils–Moscow railway and still the fast way east from the Daugava.

properties.name: Fryksdal Line
properties.highlight: Single track, no wires, up the Fryken lakes of Värmland from Kil to Torsby: railcars for people, timber and pulpwood for the mills.

properties.name: Székesfehérvár–Komárom railway
properties.highlight: Single track and still unelectrified, running from the Danube crossing at Komárom south through the Vértes foothills to Székesfehérvár.

properties.name: Thy Line
properties.highlight: Denmark's north-west corner by rail: 73 km from the fjord port of Struer through Thy to Thisted, open since 1882.

properties.name: Daugavpils–Indra railway
properties.highlight: Unelectrified 1,520 mm single track south-east from Daugavpils to Indra, the only direct rail link between Latvia and Belarus.

properties.name: Angoulême–Saintes line
properties.highlight: Down the Charente from Angoulême toward Saintes and the Atlantic, opened in 1867 through Cognac and its cellars.

properties.name: Mühldorf–Freilassing railway
properties.highlight: The south-east Bavarian cross-link of 1908, from the Salzburg border at Freilassing over the Alz and Salzach country to Mühldorf.

properties.name: Sopron–Szombathely railway
properties.highlight: GYSEV's own line along the Austrian border since 1865, linking Szombathely to Sopron in the corner of Hungary that voted to stay.

properties.name: Riihimäki–Lahti railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1869 as the first stretch of the Riihimäki–Saint Petersburg railway, and still the connection from the Helsinki main line east to Lahti.

properties.name: Kouvola–Kotka railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1890 down the Kymi river to the Gulf of Finland, ending on the quays of the port of Kotka.

properties.name: Reims-Laon railway
properties.highlight: 52 km across the Champagne vineyards and the Chemin des Dames country, from Reims to the cathedral on the hill at Laon.

properties.name: Perpignan–Villefranche line
properties.highlight: Up the Têt from the Mediterranean at Perpignan into the Pyrenean foothills, ending where the metre-gauge Train Jaune takes over at Villefranche.

properties.name: Brig–Domodossola railway
properties.highlight: The Swiss–Italian side of the Simplon: 41 km from Brig to Domodossola, almost half of it inside the 19.8 km Simplon Tunnel of 1906.

properties.name: Saintes–Royan line
properties.highlight: Half an hour down the Seudre country from Saintes to the Atlantic resort of Royan, a branch open since 1875.

properties.name: Pápa–Csorna railway
properties.highlight: A slow 1896 branch across the Kisalföld between the junction at Csorna and the baroque town of Pápa.

properties.name: Kochelsee Railway
properties.highlight: Bavarian lakes branch of 1865: from Tutzing on the Starnberger See south to the Kochelsee under the first peaks of the Alps.

properties.name: Winterthur–Etzwilen railway
properties.highlight: An 1875 single track north out of Winterthur through the Thur valley wine villages to Etzwilen near the Rhine.

properties.name: Liège–Maastricht railway
properties.highlight: Down the Meuse from Liège to Maastricht, a cross-border run open since 1861 and now worked by Arriva's Dutch regional trains.

properties.name: Sevnica–Trebnje railway
properties.highlight: Built in 1938 over the hills of Dolenjska, joining the Ljubljana–Novo mesto line at Trebnje to the Sava valley at Sevnica.

properties.name: Rheinfall railway
properties.highlight: Named for what it passes: the 1857 line from Winterthur to Schaffhausen runs along the Rhine Falls, Europe's widest waterfall.

properties.name: Monza–Molteno railway
properties.highlight: Brianza branch of 1911 climbing gently from Monza into the Lecco hills, twelve stops in twenty-nine kilometres.

properties.name: Colmar–Metzeral line
properties.highlight: Alsace's valley branch of 1868, from Colmar and its vineyards up the Fecht into the high Vosges at Metzeral.

properties.name: Fidenza–Fornovo railway
properties.highlight: A 1907 cut-off across the Emilian plain that lets Parma-bound freight and regional trains reach the Pontremolese line at Fornovo.

properties.name: Huttwil–Wolhusen railway
properties.highlight: Emmental single track of 1895, running from Huttwil down to the Little Emme and the junction at Wolhusen.

properties.name: Magdeburg-Wittenberge railway
properties.highlight: Double track and electrified across the Altmark, opened in 1849 by the Magdeburg-Wittenberge company and among the oldest railways in Germany.

properties.name: Siena–Grosseto railway
properties.highlight: Southern Tuscany at walking pace: 100 km through the Crete Senesi and the Maremma from Siena down to Grosseto, open since 1864.

properties.name: Człuchów–Słosinko railway
properties.highlight: PKP line 413 across the Pomeranian lakes and forests, capped at 50 km/h: an hour and a half for 84 km.

properties.name: Kiel–Lübeck railway
properties.highlight: Mostly single track and still without wires, joining the only two cities in Schleswig-Holstein with more than 100,000 people.

properties.name: Haapamäki–Jyväskylä railway
properties.highlight: Single track east from the Haapamäki junction to Jyväskylä, opened in 1897 through the lakes of central Finland.

properties.name: Bad Kleinen–Rostock railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1850 by the Mecklenburg Railway Company and now part of the electrified main line that carries Berlin and Hamburg trains to the Baltic at Rostock.

properties.name: Manzanares–Ciudad Real line
properties.highlight: Single Iberian-gauge track across La Mancha, opened in 1861 by the MZA company and electrified today as Adif's line 522.

properties.name: Paar Valley Railway
properties.highlight: The Paartalbahn: 63 km of single unelectrified main line from Augsburg through Friedberg, Aichach and Schrobenhausen to Ingolstadt.

properties.name: Saint-Étienne–Lyon railway
properties.highlight: Continental Europe's first railway line, built by Marc and Camille Seguin between 1828 and 1833 to bring Loire coal down to the Rhône.

properties.name: Ammersee Railway
properties.highlight: The Ammerseebahn, single track from Mering near Augsburg past Geltendorf and the Ammersee to Weilheim under the Bavarian Alps.

properties.name: Haller Willem
properties.highlight: The Haller Willem climbs the Teutoburg Forest on a gradient built in 1886; the tunnel that would have eased it was left out to save money.

properties.name: Lunéville–Saint-Dié line
properties.highlight: Fifty km of electrified single track up the Meurthe into the Vosges, never doubled because, unlike its neighbours, it carried no strategic traffic.

properties.name: Broye Line
properties.highlight: Single track across Romandy's Broye valley, crossing its sister line at Payerne on the way from Lake Neuchâtel to Fribourg.

properties.name: Österlen Line
properties.highlight: Rebuilt from two closed Skåne railways and reopened in 2003, electrified and single track along the Österlen coast to Simrishamn.

properties.name: Neumarkt-Sankt Veit–Landshut railway
properties.highlight: Single track and unelectrified down the Vils valley from Neumarkt-Sankt Veit to the Isar at Landshut, open since 1883.

properties.name: Olsztyn–Ełk railway
properties.highlight: Across Masuria through Szczytno and Pisz: the old East Prussian line from Allenstein to Lyck, still one train's ride end to end.

properties.name: Vilnius–Turmantas railway
properties.highlight: Part of the 1862 Saint Petersburg–Warsaw railway, running north from Vilnius past Ignalina's lakes to the Latvian border at Turmantas.

properties.name: Heath Railway
properties.highlight: The Heidebahn crosses the Lüneburg Heath from Hanover to Buchholz: single track, no wires, and one of only two railways of any weight on the heath.

properties.name: Amiens–Laon railway
properties.highlight: Double track the whole way and still without wires, running east from Amiens through Tergnier to the hill town of Laon since 1857.

properties.name: Vilnius–Marcinkonys railway
properties.highlight: Another surviving arm of the Warsaw–Saint Petersburg railway, single track down through the Dzūkija pine forests to Marcinkonys.

properties.name: Tartu-Koidula railway
properties.highlight: One train a day each way in winter across Põlvamaa to the border station at Koidula; in summer the service carries on to Piusa.

properties.name: Elron
properties.highlight: How Estonian trains reach Latvia: the Baltic Railway’s 1887 branch to Valga, built to meet the Riga line, and the Riga train still runs on it.

properties.name: Lübeck–Lüneburg railway
properties.highlight: Single track, unelectrified, opened in sections between 1851 and 1864: one of Germany's oldest railways, from the Elbe salt town to the Baltic.

properties.name: Line 166 (Athus–Meuse)
properties.highlight: Up the Meuse and over the Ardennes from Dinant to Bertrix: passenger trains on the Athus–Meuse freight road between Antwerp and Basel.

properties.name: Valencia–Alicante line
properties.highlight: The Iberian-gauge coastal alternative to the AVE: 1,668 mm single track through Xàtiva and Villena, still worked end to end by the Euromed.

properties.name: Alicante–Murcia line
properties.highlight: Iberian gauge since 1884, threading the Elche palm groves and the Segura valley between two provincial capitals in under an hour.

properties.name: Xàtiva–Alcoi railway
properties.highlight: Iberian-gauge single track opened in 1904, climbing 64 km of viaducts and tunnels from the Xàtiva plain into the mountains at Alcoi.

properties.name: Gäu Railway
properties.highlight: The Stuttgart end of the Gäubahn, built by the Württemberg and Baden state railways and still the through road toward Zurich.

properties.name: Kalwaria Zebrzydowska–Bielsko-Biała railway
properties.highlight: Built as the Kaiser Ferdinand Northern Railway's Bielitz–Kalwaria local line, running through Wadowice under the Beskids.

properties.name: Eiderstedt Line
properties.highlight: Out along the Eiderstedt peninsula through Tönning and Garding to the North Sea beach at Sankt Peter-Ording, on track laid in 1854.

properties.name: Clisson–Cholet line
properties.highlight: Follows the Sèvre Nantaise east from Clisson to Cholet, 39 km of single unelectrified track joining two north–south main lines.

properties.name: Münster–Rheine railway
properties.highlight: Double track and electrified across the Münsterland, opened by the Royal Westphalian Railway Company in 1856.

properties.name: Donauwörth–Treuchtlingen railway
properties.highlight: Double track over the Franconian Jura, part of the trans-European core network and of the Munich–Augsburg–Nuremberg main road.

properties.name: Lauter Valley Railway
properties.highlight: The Lautertalbahn follows its river out of Kaiserslautern to Lauterecken, a branch the Bundesbahn planned to close in the 1980s and never did.

properties.name: Lutterbach–Kruth line
properties.highlight: Up the Thur valley from Mulhouse through Thann to Kruth in the high Vosges, worked by SNCF trains and the Mulhouse tram-train together.

properties.name: Appenzell Line
properties.highlight: Metre-gauge adhesion track from Gossau up through Appenzell to Wasserauen under the Alpstein, running continuously since 1949.

properties.name: Neckarelz–Osterburken railway
properties.highlight: Opened in 1866 as part of the Baden Odenwald Railway from Heidelberg to Würzburg, now double track and electrified along the edge of the Odenwald.

properties.name: Marktoberdorf–Füssen railway
properties.highlight: The Allgäu branch to Füssen, opened by a private local railway in 1889 and now the train that delivers visitors below Neuschwanstein.

properties.name: Brașov–Zărnești railway
properties.highlight: A Transylvanian branch across the Burzenland from Brașov to Zărnești, under the limestone wall of the Piatra Craiului.

properties.name: Rostock–Tessin railway
properties.highlight: What is left of the 1895 branch east of Rostock: trains still run to Tessin, while the track on to Tribsees has been lifted.

properties.name: Deister Railway
properties.highlight: The Deisterbahn of 1872 skirts the wooded Deister ridge west of Hanover, now worked as a link in the city's S-Bahn.

properties.name: Tüßling–Burghausen railway
properties.highlight: A short Bavarian branch to the Salzach and the longest castle complex in the world at Burghausen.

properties.name: Lausanne–Vallorbe line
properties.highlight: The climb from Lake Geneva into the Jura at Vallorbe: since 1870 the shortest rail route between Paris and Milan.

properties.name: Thessaloniki–Florina
properties.highlight: West on the 1894 Salonika–Monastir line: orchard country past Veroia, Edessa of the waterfalls, then the high lakes plateau to Florina.

properties.name: Proastiakos Patras Π2
properties.highlight: Eight metre-gauge kilometres north along the Gulf of Patras to Rio, under the cables of the Rio–Antirrio bridge, on track reopened for the suburban in July 2010.

properties.name: Proastiakos Patras Π1
properties.highlight: West out of Patras on the old metre-gauge Pyrgos line, running the beach villages of the Achaean coast to Kato Achaia, which got its trains back in February 2020.

properties.name: Sevilla–Huelva
properties.highlight: The 1880 MZA line west over the Guadalquivir plain and Condado vineyards to the Atlantic at Huelva, whose neo-Mudéjar terminus has stood empty since 2019 and lost its roof to a fire in 2022.

properties.name: Ballina Branch
properties.highlight: Mayo’s surviving branch: half an hour down the Moy valley from Ballina to Manulla Junction, meeting the Dublin trains on the Westport line.

properties.name: Limerick–Waterford
properties.highlight: Ireland’s quiet cross-country line of 1854: a change of trains at Limerick Junction, then the Suir valley through Cahir and Clonmel to Waterford.

properties.name: Limerick–Ballybrophy
properties.highlight: The Nenagh branch, joined up in 1864: along the Shannon past Castleconnell’s rapids, then North Tipperary farmland through Nenagh and Roscrea to the mainline junction at Ballybrophy. Two through trains a day.

properties.name: Leeds–Morecambe
properties.highlight: The 1850 “Little North Western” the slow way out of Airedale: Bentham’s fell country, the Lune valley at Wennington, and the sands of Morecambe Bay to finish.

properties.name: Athens–Chalkida
properties.highlight: Athens’s other suburban artery: up the mainline past Oinoi, then the 1904 branch down to the Euripus strait at Chalkida, the gateway to Evia.

properties.name: Proastiakos Airport Line
properties.highlight: Port to plane on one ticket: from Piraeus through central Athens, then east along the Attiki Odos motorway median to the airport at Spata.

properties.name: Shrewsbury–Chester
properties.highlight: The 1848 border line between two walled towns: over Telford’s country at Chirk and the great Cefn viaduct, down the Dee valley through Wrexham to Chester.

properties.name: Málaga–Sevilla
properties.highlight: The slow way between Andalucía’s two great cities: up the Guadalhorce past El Chorro’s gorge, beneath the Caminito del Rey walkway, then across the campiña by Osuna and Marchena.

properties.name: Almería–Granada
properties.highlight: Across the high desert of the Hoya de Guadix: Almería’s palms to Granada by way of Moreda, through the badlands the spaghetti Westerns loved.

properties.name: Jaén–Cádiz
properties.highlight: One train across all Andalucía: olive country at Jaén, the Guadalquivir at Córdoba and Seville, sherry country at Jerez, and the Atlantic at Cádiz.

properties.name: Jaén–Madrid
properties.highlight: The classic climb out of Andalucía: through the Despeñaperros gorge, the old gateway pass, then straight across La Mancha to Madrid.

properties.name: Sevilla–Zafra
properties.highlight: North out of Seville into the Sierra Morena: cork oaks and mining country by Cazalla and Llerena to the junction town of Zafra.

properties.name: West Wales Line
properties.highlight: The 1856 line west: Llanelli’s sands, the Tywi at Carmarthen, then deep Pembrokeshire to the haven Nelson called the finest port in Christendom.

properties.name: Pembroke Dock Branch
properties.highlight: Branch line to the sea at every turn: Tenby’s walls and beaches, Saundersfoot, and the Cleddau at Pembroke Dock.

properties.name: Fishguard Harbour Line
properties.highlight: The boat train’s line since 1906: over the Preseli foothills to Fishguard Harbour, where the ferry sails for the Rosslare this atlas draws from the Irish side.

properties.name: Rhymney Line
properties.highlight: The Rhymney Railway’s own valley, opened to passengers in March 1858: out of Cardiff through the Caerphilly tunnel under the mountain, then Ystrad Mynach and Bargoed to the head of the valley at Rhymney.

properties.name: Ebbw Vale Line
properties.highlight: A coal line carrying people again: passenger trains ended in 1962, came back to Ebbw Vale Parkway in February 2008 and reached Ebbw Vale Town in May 2015, climbing the Ebbw valley off the Newport main line.

properties.name: Maesteg Line
properties.highlight: West along the South Wales main line to Bridgend, then up the Llynfi valley on Llynvi and Ogmore metals through Tondu to Maesteg. Reopened to passengers in 1992, twenty-two years after the last train.

properties.name: Vale of Glamorgan Line
properties.highlight: The coast road to Bridgend: through Barry and out along the Glamorgan shore past Rhoose, where the airport is, and Llantwit Major. Passenger trains stopped in June 1964 and returned in June 2005 with two new stations.

properties.name: Borderlands Line
properties.highlight: Wrexham to the Wirral: 1860s Wrexham, Mold and Connah’s Quay metals joined to the 1896 North Wales and Liverpool line, crossing the Dee on the Hawarden swing bridge and running on to Bidston for Liverpool.

properties.name: EuroCity Zürich–München
properties.highlight: Electrified through in 2020, which cut an hour off the run: out of Zurich by Winterthur and St Gallen, over the Rhine at St Margrethen, along Lake Constance through Bregenz and Lindau, then the Allgäu to Munich.

properties.name: Intercity Vlissingen
properties.highlight: The long way to the sea: Haarlem, Leiden, The Hague and Rotterdam, then over the Hollands Diep into Zeeland and along the Scheldt through Goes and Middelburg to Vlissingen, on rails finished in 1873.

properties.name: Bucharest–Sofia
properties.highlight: Two capitals in a day: south from Bucharest to the Danube, over the 1954 Friendship Bridge at Giurgiu into Ruse, then across the Bulgarian plain by Gorna Oryahovitsa and Pleven to Sofia.

properties.name: EIC Warszawa–Szczecin
properties.highlight: Warsaw to the Oder in four and a quarter hours, on the old Prussian main line west through Poznań, then Krzyż and Stargard to Szczecin, where Poland meets the German border.

properties.name: Sofia–Vidin
properties.highlight: Up the Iskar gorge, which is the reason to take it: the river cuts a canyon north out of Sofia through Svoge and Lakatnik to Mezdra, then Vratsa and the plain to the Danube at Vidin.

properties.name: Kyiv–Chernivtsi
properties.highlight: Overnight across western Ukraine: out of Kyiv just before nine, Lviv in the small hours, then Ivano-Frankivsk and Kolomyia to Chernivtsi by breakfast, ending on the Habsburg line of 1866.

properties.name: Intercity Den Helder–Nijmegen
properties.highlight: Coast to the German border in one train: from Den Helder at the tip of North Holland through Alkmaar and Amsterdam, then Utrecht, the edge of the Veluwe and Arnhem to Nijmegen on the Waal.

properties.name: Zagreb–Vinkovci
properties.highlight: East across Slavonia on the old Zagreb to Belgrade main line: out through Dugo Selo, the Sava plain by Novska and Slavonski Brod, then the oak country beyond Đakovo to Vinkovci.

properties.name: Linha de Guimarães
properties.highlight: Metre gauge until 2004, when it was rebuilt to Iberian gauge and wired: out of Porto through Ermesinde and up the Ave valley by Trofa and Santo Tirso to Guimarães, where Portugal was founded.

properties.name: IC Antwerpen–Hasselt
properties.highlight: An hour east from the Scheldt to the Demer: out of Antwerp through Lier, then Heist-op-den-Berg and Diest across the Campine to Hasselt, on rails joined up in the 1860s.

properties.name: Javelin North Kent
properties.highlight: The other Javelin to Margate: off HS1 at Ebbsfleet onto the 1846 North Kent line, past Rochester’s castle and cathedral, Faversham’s breweries, then the seaside string of Whitstable, Herne Bay and Margate.

properties.name: Østfoldbanen: Oslo–Ski
properties.highlight: The original 1879 Østfold line out of Oslo, hugging the fjord shore through Nordstrand and Ljan before climbing the ridge to Ski, now the all stations companion to the Blix tunnel bored beneath it.

properties.name: Østre linje
properties.highlight: Norway’s 1882 eastern line: through the Blix tunnel to Ski in eleven minutes, then out across the grain fields and timber towns of indre Østfold, calling at Askim and Mysen on the way to Rakkestad.

properties.name: Bratsbergbanen
properties.highlight: Built in 1917 to carry Norsk Hydro’s fertiliser from the Notodden works to the sea, the Bratsberg line climbs from the Telemark canal towns past Skien and crosses the Sørland main line at Nordagutu.

properties.name: R10 Krakonoš
properties.highlight: Rychlík from Prague across the Elbe lowlands to Hradec Králové, then up the foothills to Trutnov beneath the Krkonoše mountains.

properties.name: RegioJet R8
properties.highlight: RegioJet’s yellow trains on the R8: through the Moravian Gate via Přerov, on rails the Nordbahn laid toward Bohumín in 1847.

properties.name: IC Warszawa–Lublin
properties.highlight: The 1877 Vistula River Railroad east from Warsaw, rebuilt for 160 km/h: under two hours to Lublin’s renaissance old town.

properties.name: IC Warszawa–Olsztyn
properties.highlight: Off the Gdańsk main line at Działdowo, then through the wooded lake country via Nidzica and Olsztynek into Olsztyn, gateway to Masuria.

properties.name: IC Brda
properties.highlight: The 1862 Warsaw–Bydgoszcz Railway via the brick-gothic city of Toruń, Copernicus’s birthplace, to the Brda riverside.

properties.name: Nadodrzanka
properties.highlight: The Nadodrzanka: down the Oder valley through Głogów and Zielona Góra, the quiet 1870s corridor between Silesia and the Baltic.

properties.name: R Urpín
properties.highlight: Named for the hill above Banská Bystrica: the southern rychlík route via Levice and Zvolen into the heart of central Slovakia.

properties.name: Zvolen–Košice railway
properties.highlight: The southern trans-Slovak line: three hours through the karst country via Lučenec, Plešivec and Rožňava beneath medieval mining towns.

properties.name: Railjet Wien–Venezia
properties.highlight: One seat Vienna to Venice: over the Semmering, through the new Koralm tunnel to Klagenfurt and Villach, then the 1879 Pontebbana across the Julian Alps.

properties.name: EC Wien–Ljubljana
properties.highlight: The EuroCity to Slovenia on the 1857 Southern Railway: over the Semmering to Graz, the Drava at Maribor, then the Sava valley into Ljubljana.

properties.name: IC Köln–Norddeich
properties.highlight: DB’s seaside Intercity: down the Rhine-Ruhr, through Münster and the Emsland flats to the North Sea pier at Norddeich Mole.

properties.name: R9 Vysočina
properties.highlight: The slow way to Brno: the 1953-completed Vysočina highland line via Havlíčkův Brod and Žďár, the second main line between the two cities.

properties.name: Silesian Mountain Railway
properties.highlight: The 1867 Silesian Mountain Railway: through Wałbrzych’s coal valleys and Jelenia Góra, climbing to nearly 700 m at Szklarska Poręba under the Karkonosze.

properties.name: Košice–Humenné railway
properties.highlight: Eastern Slovakia’s REX corridor via Trebišov toward the Vihorlat hills; the Humenné sleeper from Prague finishes on the same rails.

properties.name: Kék Hullám
properties.highlight: The Kék Hullám (Blue Wave) IC along Balaton’s vineyard-clad north shore: Balatonfüred, the basalt hills of Badacsony, then inland to Tapolca.

properties.name: ICE Frankfurt–Dresden
properties.highlight: The Saxony ICE: Fulda’s wooded hills, Luther’s Eisenach and Erfurt, the 2015 high-speed line into Leipzig, then the Elbe plain to Dresden.

properties.name: IC Karlsruhe–Nürnberg
properties.highlight: The cross-country IC via the 1861 Remsbahn: Stuttgart, the Rems valley vineyards, then Aalen and Crailsheim’s hills to Nuremberg.

properties.name: IC Poznań–Gdynia
properties.highlight: Across Wielkopolska and Pomerania: Gniezno’s cathedral hill, Bydgoszcz, then the Vistula crossing at Tczew and the Tri-City coast to Gdynia.

properties.name: Braunschweig–Uelzen railway
properties.highlight: The emigrants’ road: Braunschweig via Gifhorn to Uelzen, on to the America ships at Bremen and Hamburg; single track since the war, never wired, famously Germany’s most delayed line.

properties.name: Outback Xplorer
properties.highlight: Weekly railcar over the Blue Mountains and out past Parkes into the saltbush: thirteen hours from Sydney Central to the silver town on the South Australian border.

properties.name: Tshiuetin
properties.highlight: The Labrador iron road with no highway beside it: twice a week from the St Lawrence at Sept-Îles to Schefferville, on the first railway in North America owned and run by First Nations.

properties.name: Ravenglass & Eskdale Railway
properties.highlight: Fifteen-inch gauge up Eskdale from the Cumbrian coast, laid for iron ore in 1875 and run since as a miniature main line that Cumbria calls La’al Ratty.

properties.name: Kandertalbahn
properties.highlight: Sunday steam up the Kandertal from the Rhine plain at Haltingen to Kandern, the 1895 branch kept running by the society that saved it.

properties.name: Mátravasút (Mátra Forest Railway)
properties.highlight: Seven-sixty gauge out of Gyöngyös into the Mátra hills: a 1920s timber railway carrying holidaymakers to Mátrafüred behind an Mk48 in open-sided coaches.

properties.name: ICE Hamburg–Binz
properties.highlight: The Rügen through train: out of Hamburg past Schwerin and Rostock to Stralsund, over the Rügendamm and on to the chalk coast at Binz.

properties.name: ICE Dortmund–Oberstdorf
properties.highlight: The Ruhr to the Allgäu in one train: Dortmund, the Rhine gorge past the Lorelei, Mannheim and Ulm, then up the Iller valley to Oberstdorf under the Alps.

properties.name: IC Gera–Düsseldorf
properties.highlight: East Thuringia to the Rhine: Gera and Jena, Erfurt and Eisenach under the Wartburg, then Kassel, the Ruhr and Düsseldorf.

properties.name: IC Leipzig–Norddeich
properties.highlight: Saxony to the North Sea ferry pier: Leipzig, Magdeburg and Hannover, then Bremen and the East Frisian flats to the quayside at Norddeich Mole.

properties.name: IC Leipzig–Warnemünde
properties.highlight: Leipzig to the Baltic beach: Halle and Magdeburg, the Stendal cut-off and Schwerin, then Rostock and out to the pier at Warnemünde.

properties.name: EN Slovakia / Chopin
properties.highlight: Overnight between two capitals: out of Prague past Pardubice and Olomouc, over the border to Katowice, then the fast Central Trunk line into Warsaw by breakfast.

properties.name: Eurotunnel Le Shuttle
properties.highlight: Drive on at Folkestone, drive off at Calais: thirty five minutes under the Channel on the shuttle that carries the cars, and the only fixed link between Britain and the continent.

properties.name: Vereina Car Shuttle
properties.highlight: Metre gauge under the Silvretta: cars loaded at Selfranga near Klosters and carried through the 19 km Vereina tunnel to the Engadine, open when the Flüela pass is shut.

properties.name: Tauernschleuse
properties.highlight: Salzburg to Carinthia without the pass: the car shuttle through the 1909 Tauern tunnel, hourly under the Alpine main ridge from Böckstein to Mallnitz.

properties.name: EC Wawel
properties.highlight: The EuroCity across Poland: Berlin and the Oder, Wrocław and Opole, the Silesian cities and Kraków, then on east to Przemyśl at the Ukrainian border.

properties.name: Bregenzerwaldbahn (Wälderbähnle)
properties.highlight: All that is left of the 760 mm line to Bregenz: five kilometres of the Wälderbähnle between Bezau and Schwarzenberg, worked by steam and diesel through the Bregenzerwald on summer weekends.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: West Flanders end to end: out of the dunes at De Panne past Veurne and Diksmuide, then Tielt and Deinze to Ghent, on the line that finally reached the coast in 1870.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: East across the Campine heath from Antwerp, through Lier, Herentals, Geel and Mol to Hamont in the far corner of Limburg, on rails completed in 1879.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: Flanders’ two great cities in an hour, straight through the Waasland at Sint-Niklaas and Lokeren, on a line that reached Ghent in 1847 but Antwerp’s own stations only in 1970, through the Kennedy tunnel under the Scheldt.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: The long way to the sea: from the airport out to Denderleeuw, then Oudenaarde, Kortrijk and Roeselare through the Flemish Ardennes before Bruges and Ostend.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: Down the oldest railway on the Continent, Brussels to Mechelen in 1835, then the 1843 line south past Nivelles into the Sambre coalfield at Charleroi.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: Forty-six minutes down the Meuse, Liège to Namur under the cliffs and citadels of the valley, on the line the Namur to Liège company opened along the riverbank in 1850.

properties.name: IC Warszawa–Terespol
properties.highlight: Warsaw east to the Bug on the 1866 Terespol railway, the third line built in Congress Poland, running through Siedlce and Biała Podlaska to the Belarusian frontier.

properties.name: Piła–Szczecin railway
properties.highlight: Across Pomerania on a railway the Prussians finished in 1895 and Poland gave up on in 2000: through trains came back to Wałcz and Choszczno in 2012, five pairs a day.

properties.name: Szczecin–Świnoujście railway
properties.highlight: Szczecin to the Baltic across Wolin island, over the Dziwna and through Międzyzdroje to the ferry berths at Świnoujście, on rails that reached the Świna in 1900.

properties.name: IC Olsztyn–Elbląg
properties.highlight: Warmia end to end, Olsztyn through Morąg to Elbląg and the Vistula Lagoon, on a line that reached Olsztyn from Bogaczewo in August 1883.

properties.name: Inowrocław–Olsztyn railway
properties.highlight: Kuyavia to Masuria across the Vistula at Toruń, then Iława and Ostróda to Olsztyn, on the Prussian trunk that joined Poznań to East Prussia in 1873.

properties.name: Sierpc–Nowy Dwór railway
properties.highlight: A Mazovian branch line: Sierpc down the Wkra valley to Nasielsk, then Modlin and Nowy Dwór, on a First World War military narrow gauge regauged and opened properly in 1924.

properties.name: Lublin–Zamość railway
properties.highlight: Lublin south east to Zamość and its Renaissance old town, through Rejowiec and the Wieprz valley, on the section of the Rejowiec to Hrebenne line opened in 1916.

properties.name: Katowice–Zwardoń railway
properties.highlight: Out of the Silesian coalfield into the Beskids: Katowice through Tychy and Bielsko-Biała to Żywiec and the Slovak border at Zwardoń, a line completed piece by piece to 1912.

properties.name: Dęblin–Łuków railway
properties.highlight: Dęblin to Łuków across the Lublin plain, on rails that took sixty years to join up: Łuków reached Stawy in 1876 and the last stretch into Dęblin waited until 1935.

properties.name: Kutno–Płock railway
properties.highlight: Kutno north to Płock and the Vistula, on a line opened on the last day of 1925, the bridge over the river into the city following in 1938.

properties.name: RE 3 Dresden–Hof
properties.highlight: Saxony corner to corner: out of Dresden up the Tharandt ramp, then Freiberg, Chemnitz, Zwickau and the Vogtland to Hof, on a chain of lines the Freiberg link joined up in 1869.

properties.name: RE 6 Chemnitz–Leipzig
properties.highlight: An hour between Saxony’s two biggest cities, Chemnitz to Leipzig by way of Geithain and Borna, on a line opened in April 1872.

properties.name: RB 45 Chemnitz–Elsterwerda
properties.highlight: North out of Chemnitz down the Zschopau valley to Döbeln and Riesa on the Elbe, then on to Elsterwerda, joining a railway of 1852 to one of 1875.

properties.name: RB 1 Zwickau–Kraslice
properties.highlight: Out of the Zwickau coalfield into the Vogtland hills and over the Czech border above Klingenthal to Kraslice, on rails a coal railway company opened in November 1875.

properties.name: RB 59 Gammertingen–Schelklingen
properties.highlight: Across the Swabian Alb at sixty kilometres an hour: Gammertingen to Engstingen and Münsingen, then down to Schelklingen and the Danube, on branch lines opened in 1901.

properties.name: R-1 Madrid–Ávila
properties.highlight: Out of Madrid past El Escorial and over the Guadarrama to Ávila and its complete medieval walls, on the main line to the French border built between 1860 and 1864.

properties.name: Oradea–Püspökladány railway
properties.highlight: Over the Hungarian border on rails the Tisza Railway Company put into service on 22 April 1858, still the way out of Oradea onto the Great Plain at Püspökladány.

properties.name: Hanko line
properties.highlight: Finland’s first private railway, opened in 1873 and paid for by St Petersburg merchants who wanted an ice free winter port: forty minutes down the branch from Karjaa to Hanko.

properties.name: RE 2 Liberec–Dresden
properties.highlight: Bohemia into Saxony on the Lusatian branches: Liberec down the Neisse to Zittau, then Ebersbach and Bischofswerda, on a chain the Oberoderwitz link completed in October 1879.

properties.name: S6 Lienz–Villach
properties.highlight: Down the Drau from East Tyrol into Carinthia, Lienz past Oberdrauburg and Spittal to Villach, on the original Drautalbahn of 20 November 1871: an S-Bahn since 2015, renumbered S6 in December 2025.

properties.name: S4 Villach–Hermagor
properties.highlight: South out of Villach to Arnoldstein, then west up the Gail valley to Hermagor, on a branch opened on 11 August 1894 and ridden by 310 people on its first train.

properties.name: Tunis–Annaba
properties.train: SNCFT first and second class coaches
properties.highlight: Tunis to Béja, Jendouba and Ghardimaou, then over the border to Souk Ahras and Annaba: the 1884 Bône-Guelma link, silent from 1995 until the first train ran again on 11 August 2024.

properties.name: Nanning–Hanoi International
properties.highlight: Out of Nanning by night through Chongzuo and Pingxiang, over the border at Đồng Đăng, down to Gia Lâm in Hanoi: through since 1955, stopped in 2020, running again from 25 May 2025.

properties.name: Pitești–Craiova railway
properties.highlight: Opened on 9 May 1878, six years after the line from Bucharest had reached Pitești, and still an unelectrified single track running west across the Olt to Craiova.

properties.name: Varna–Shumen railway
properties.highlight: The last 24 km into Shumen opened on 20 June 1895; everything east of Kaspichan is the first railway built in what is now Bulgaria, the Ruse to Varna line of 1866.

properties.name: Niš–Zaječar railway
properties.highlight: The Timok valley line, finished in 1922 by Russian emigre labour through nineteen tunnels in the Svrljig gorge, and still the only rail link between Niš and the eastern border country.

properties.name: R Zakarpatia
properties.highlight: The daily crossing out of Transcarpathia into the European gauge, over the Tisza at Cierna nad Tisou on a line whose last section opened on 22 October 1873.

properties.name: Kraljevo–Rudnica railway
properties.highlight: Up the Ibar valley past Mataruska Banja and Josanicka Banja, on rails completed in 1931 to carry ore north out of the Ibar mines, and the only atlas line for a hundred kilometres in any direction.

properties.name: Chiltern Main Line
properties.highlight: The other main line from London to Birmingham: finished in 1910, when the Bicester cut-off shortened it by thirty kilometres and let the Great Western match its rival on two hours.

properties.name: West Coastway line
properties.highlight: Five companies built this coast road in rails between 1840 and 1889; the last of it runs out over the water on piles into Portsmouth Harbour, opened on 2 October 1876.

properties.name: Hatvan–Somoskőújfalu railway
properties.highlight: Coal from Salgótarján is why it exists: Hatvan to the pits opened on 9 May 1867, and the single track on through Somoskőújfalu to Losonc followed in 1871.

properties.name: L2 Děčín–Liberec
properties.highlight: Four companies laid it in pieces from 1869 onwards; the last link opened on 16 September 1900, climbing to Liberec through five tunnels and over the 30 m viaduct at Novina.

properties.name: Monforte de Lemos–A Coruña railway
properties.highlight: For seventy years the only railway between Galicia and the meseta: Lugo to A Coruña opened on 10 October 1875, and the last stretch east of Monforte on 4 September 1883.

properties.name: Baja–Kiskunhalas railway
properties.highlight: Trianon cut two branch lines in half and Hungary joined the stumps: the Baja end opened on 8 January 1885, the Kiskunhalas end on 31 October 1903.

properties.name: Skövde–Nässjö railway
properties.highlight: The Jönköpingsbanan was the Southern main line’s own way north, finished on 1 December 1864; ten years later a shorter line through Katrineholm took its traffic away.

properties.name: Sierpc–Toruń railway
properties.highlight: One of the last railways the Second Republic built: eighty kilometres laid between 1935 and 1937, and the Drwęca bridge at Lubicz was the first in Poland to carry welded girders.

properties.name: Varna–Burgas railway
properties.highlight: Begun in 1916, abandoned, and finished in the war: Karnobat to Komunari opened in 1942 and the last stretch down the Kamchia valley in 1943, joining Bulgaria’s two Black Sea cities directly.

properties.name: Valladolid–Puebla de Sanabria railway
properties.highlight: Thirty years of building, some of it by Republican prisoners at forced labour: the climb from Zamora to Puebla de Sanabria opened on 23 September 1952.

properties.name: Fossano–San Giuseppe di Cairo railway
properties.highlight: The 1874 road to Savona ran the long way round through Bra; this double track shortcut by way of Mondovì and Ceva replaced it in 1933.

properties.name: Donauuferbahn
properties.highlight: Mauthausen to Grein opened on 4 July 1898 and the state line on through the Strudengau in 1909; trains now turn at St. Nikola-Struden, where the rest of the Danube line was given up in 2019.

properties.name: Békéscsaba–Salonta railway
properties.highlight: The Alföld to Fiume company opened it on 14 September 1871 and then went broke; Trianon cut the line in two, but nobody lifted the rails and the crossing still works.

properties.name: Číčenice–Nové Údolí railway
properties.highlight: Prachatice was reached in 1893, Volary in 1899 and the Bavarian border in 1910; through trains to Passau stopped in 1951 and the rails past Nové Údolí are now pushed by hand.

properties.name: Évora–Beja railway
properties.highlight: Two railways of the 1860s meet at Casa Branca: the branch up to Évora opened on 14 September 1863, and the main line reached Beja on 15 February 1864.

properties.name: Almtalbahn
properties.highlight: Wels built it to keep the Almtal from Lambach: the branch from Sattledt opened in 1901, owned by a local company until 1942 and run by the state railway from the first day.

properties.name: Neusiedler Seebahn
properties.highlight: It opened on 19 December 1897 with all 109 km of it inside Hungary; Trianon moved the northern part into Austria in 1921, and trains have crossed the border at Pamhagen ever since.

properties.name: Biella–Novara railway
properties.highlight: Mussolini opened it on 18 May 1939 and no train ran for fourteen months, because the rolling stock was not ready; promised electric in 1925, it never was, and the state took it over in 1961.

properties.name: Chivasso–Casale Monferrato railway
properties.highlight: A third class line under the Baccarini law of 1879, built to reach the Monferrato from the main line at Chivasso: the stretch from Castelrosso to Casale Popolo opened on 30 April 1887.

properties.name: Markarydsbanan
properties.highlight: The Southern main line nearly came this way in the 1850s and went east instead; two small companies built it anyway, Hässleholm to Vittsjö in 1890 and on to Markaryd in 1892.

properties.name: Vác–Balassagyarmat railway
properties.highlight: Two railways meet at Drégelypalánk: the Ipoly valley line reached Balassagyarmat on 15 August 1891, and the line south through the Börzsöny to Vác carried its first train on 11 July 1909.

properties.name: Hausruckbahn
properties.highlight: The northern half of the Salzkammergutbahn, opened on 23 October 1877 by the Crown Prince Rudolf company to bring Hausruck coal down to the salt pans of Ebensee and Ischl.

properties.name: Innkreisbahn
properties.highlight: Neumarkt-Kallham to Braunau opened on 20 December 1870 and the bridge over the Inn to Simbach on 1 June 1871; from 1883 to 1897 the Orient Express took this way between Vienna and Munich.

properties.name: Linzer Lokalbahn
properties.highlight: Electric from the start: Waizenkirchen to Peuerbach opened in 1908, the link on to Eferding and Linz on 16 December 1912, and Stern & Hafferl have run it since 1 January 1913.

properties.name: Franz-Josefs-Bahn
properties.highlight: The first 22 km of the line to Gmünd and Prague: the Vienna end opened in 1870, once the delayed stretch in from Eggenburg was finished, and ran as part of the Stadtbahn from 1898 to 1925.

properties.name: EBOE Elmshorn–Ulzburg
properties.highlight: Elmshorn to Barmstedt opened as a light railway on 15 July 1896; the Barmstedt to Oldesloe company carried it on to Ulzburg on 9 June 1907, and the AKN has run it since 1981.

properties.name: Biel–Bern railway
properties.highlight: Bern to Zollikofen opened on 16 June 1857 as part of the Centralbahn line to Olten; the Bernese state railway carried it on over Lyss to Biel in 1864.

properties.name: Odsherredsbanen
properties.highlight: Point one of the great railway act of 1894: Holbæk county took the concession on 6 May 1896, and the line up the peninsula to Nykøbing opened on 18 May 1899.

properties.name: Østbanen
properties.highlight: The East Zealand line began service on 1 July 1879, Køge through Hårlev to the sea at Faxe Ladeplads; the trains from Køge still divide at Hårlev, one half for the coast and the other for Rødvig.

properties.name: Gribskovbanen
properties.highlight: Built in 1880 to carry timber out of the Gribskov forest as far as Græsted; the line reached the sea at Gilleleje on 14 May 1896, and its passengers have called it the Pig ever since.

properties.name: Parikkala–Savonlinna railway
properties.highlight: The Savonlinna line was built from Elisenvaara on the Karelian railway: Punkaharju was reached in November 1906 and the whole line on 1 February 1908; the junction it started from is now in Russia.

properties.name: Tjustbanan
properties.highlight: Västervik to Åtvidaberg was laid in 1879 as an 891 mm narrow gauge line; the link to Bjärka-Säby in 1906 joined it to Linköping, and the whole of it was widened to standard gauge in 1964.

properties.name: Laskowice–Czersk railway
properties.highlight: A Prussian act of 20 July 1902 ordered it, and the 55 km from Laskowice to Czersk opened on 2 October 1906; the stretch beyond to Bąk came in 1928 to feed the building of the coal trunk line.

properties.name: Czersk–Tuchola railway
properties.highlight: A piece of the coal trunk line built to reach the new port at Gdynia without crossing the Free City of Danzig: the whole Bydgoszcz to Gdynia stretch opened on 9 November 1930.

properties.name: Catania–Caltagirone railway
properties.highlight: Valsavoia to Scordia opened in November 1889 and the whole climb to Caltagirone on 31 October 1892; the 1979 extension to Gela has been shut since a viaduct collapsed, reopening promised for 2026.

properties.name: Ponitran Prievidza–Bratislava
properties.highlight: Down the Nitra valley on the StEG line of 1876 to 1896 and across to the Váh at Leopoldov on the link of 1898 that first gave Prievidza a fast train to Bratislava.

properties.name: Zaragoza–Barcelona by Caspe
properties.highlight: MZA’s second way from Zaragoza to the sea, built to cut out Lleida: Reus to Móra opened in 1891, Caspe was reached in 1893, the line was complete in 1894 and carried its first trains in 1895.

properties.name: Medgidia–Tulcea railway
properties.highlight: Begun in 1911, stopped by the war, opened to Babadag on 1 October 1925 and finished on 25 March 1938, when Tulcea, the last county town in Romania without a railway, got its first train.

properties.name: R11 České Budějovice–Brno
properties.highlight: Three railways end to end: the Franz Josef line to Veselí from 1871, the Bohemian transversal on to Jihlava from 1887, and the line through Třebíč to Brno, whose middle section opened in June 1886.

properties.name: Sp Strakonice–Tábor
properties.highlight: Opened in 1889 across South Bohemia: out of the Otava valley at Strakonice, through Písek, over the Vltava at Červená and past the stone viaducts above Milevsko to Tábor.

properties.name: Târgu Jiu–Craiova railway
properties.highlight: Filiași to Craiova is the 1878 line; the branch up the Jiu opened in two pieces in 1888, to Cărbunești and then to Târgu Jiu, which stayed the end of the railway for another 27 years.

properties.name: Palermo–Trapani railway
properties.highlight: The long way round the west of Sicily, by Castelvetrano, Mazara and Marsala: the through line was finished on 5 June 1881, and since the short route by Milo closed in 2013 it is the only one.

properties.name: Maubeuge–Charleroi railway
properties.highlight: Charleroi to the French frontier at Erquelinnes opened on 6 November 1852, and the Nord company’s line from Saint-Quentin met it there on 11 August 1855, on the old main road from Paris to Brussels.

properties.name: c2c Shoeburyness–London
properties.highlight: The Tilbury company reached Shoeburyness in 1884 and finished its direct line through Upminster to a re-sited Pitsea in 1886, the way the stopping trains from the sea to Fenchurch Street run today.

properties.name: Chiltern Marylebone–Aylesbury Vale Parkway
properties.highlight: Marylebone opened on 15 March 1899, the last main line terminus London built for a century; the train runs out over the old Metropolitan and Great Central road to a station opened on 14 December 2008.

properties.name: Dartmouth Steam Railway
properties.highlight: The Kingswear branch of 1864, sold by British Rail to the Dart Valley company in 1972: steam from Paignton over Goodrington Sands and along the Dart estuary to Kingswear, for the ferry to Dartmouth.

properties.name: North Norfolk Railway
properties.highlight: The Poppy Line: the last stretch of the Midland & Great Northern in Norfolk, carrying passengers again since July 1975, from the seaside at Sheringham past Weybourne to Holt.

properties.name: Llangollen Railway
properties.highlight: Ten miles of the Great Western’s Ruabon–Barmouth line, closed in 1965: volunteers reopened Llangollen station in 1975 and relaid the Dee valley mile by mile, reaching a new station at Corwen in 2023.

properties.name: Epping Ongar Railway
properties.highlight: The Central line’s lost end: London Underground closed Epping to Ongar in 1994, and heritage steam and diesel have run it again since 2012, from Ongar through North Weald to the edge of Epping Forest.

properties.name: Embsay & Bolton Abbey Steam Railway
properties.highlight: Four miles of the Midland’s Skipton–Ilkley line, closed in 1965 and reopened by volunteers in 1981, with trains back into Bolton Abbey station, for the priory estate, since 1997.

properties.name: Dean Forest Railway
properties.highlight: The Severn & Wye’s line into the Forest of Dean, rebuilt by volunteers: passenger trains since 1991, down to Lydney Junction in 1995 and up through the woods to Parkend.

properties.name: Lakeside & Haverthwaite Railway
properties.highlight: The Furness Railway’s 1869 branch to Windermere, reopened in 1973: three and a half miles of steam from Haverthwaite to Lakeside, where trains still connect with the lake steamers.

properties.name: Bure Valley Railway
properties.highlight: Norfolk’s 15-inch-gauge railway, laid in 1990 on the old East Norfolk trackbed: nine miles from the Broads at Wroxham, over the River Bure and under the A140 by tunnel, to Aylsham.

properties.name: Chinnor & Princes Risborough Railway
properties.highlight: A surviving piece of the Great Western’s Watlington branch at the foot of the Chilterns, reopened to passengers in 1994 and reconnected to the main line at Princes Risborough in 2016.

properties.name: Caledonian Railway (Brechin)
properties.highlight: Four miles of the Aberdeen Railway’s 1840s line between Brechin’s preserved terminus and Bridge of Dun, worked by volunteers every summer since 1993.

properties.name: Cholsey & Wallingford Railway
properties.highlight: The Great Western’s 1866 Wallingford branch, kept alive into preservation by the town’s maltings traffic: two and a half miles from Wallingford to the main line at Cholsey.

properties.name: Gwili Railway
properties.highlight: Wales’ first standard-gauge heritage railway, reopened in 1978 on the Carmarthen–Aberystwyth line, the last in Wales to lose Brunel’s broad gauge, and now four and a half miles up the Gwili valley.

properties.name: Kirklees Light Railway
properties.highlight: A 15-inch-gauge railway opened in 1991 on the Lancashire & Yorkshire’s Clayton West branch: through Skelmanthorpe and the 511-yard Shelley Woodhouse tunnel, with Emley Moor mast in view.

properties.name: Leighton Buzzard Light Railway
properties.highlight: Built in 1919 to carry sand from the Bedfordshire quarries and running passenger trains since 1968: two-foot-gauge industrial steam and diesel from Page’s Park to Stonehenge Works.

properties.name: Strathspey Railway
properties.highlight: Steam since 1978 on a preserved stretch of the Highland Railway main line, one of only a handful of former main lines saved in Britain: from Aviemore through Boat of Garten to Broomhill.

properties.name: Volk’s Electric Railway
properties.highlight: The world’s oldest operating electric railway: Magnus Volk opened it on Brighton seafront in August 1883, and its cars still run along the beach from Aquarium to Black Rock.

properties.name: Manx Electric Railway
properties.highlight: The oldest electric tramway whose original cars are still in service: 1890s tramcars on the coast line from Douglas to Laxey and, since 1899, over the cliffs to Ramsey.

properties.name: Snaefell Mountain Railway
properties.highlight: Wooden electric cars of 1895 climb five miles from Laxey to the 621 m summit of Snaefell, the Isle of Man’s highest point, braking on a Fell centre rail.

properties.name: Glenbrook Vintage Railway
properties.highlight: Steam on the old Waiuku branch south of Auckland, run by volunteers since 1977: a 7.4 km line from Glenbrook to Victoria Avenue that carries up to 30,000 passengers a season.

properties.name: Hornbækbanen
properties.highlight: North Zealand’s coast line: Elsinore out past the Øresund bathing towns to Hornbæk from 1906, and on to Gilleleje from July 1916.

properties.name: Østbanen
properties.highlight: Every station on it was drawn by Heinrich Wenck: the East Zealand line of 1879 across Stevns to the chalk cliffs at Rødvig, rebuilt and reopened in October 2024.

properties.name: Tisvildeleje branch
properties.highlight: The Gribskovbanen’s western arm: built in 1880 to bring timber out of the Gribskov forest, on to Helsinge in 1897 and to the Kattegat dunes at Tisvildeleje in 1924.

properties.name: Utrecht–Rotterdam railway
properties.highlight: The Rhenish Railway Company built it between 1855 and 1858; after the Maas station was bombed out of Rotterdam in 1940 the city end was rebuilt on an embankment and reopened in 1953.

properties.name: Santhià–Biella railway
properties.highlight: Inaugurated on 8 September 1856 with the public works minister aboard the special from Turin: 27 km down from the Biellese wool towns to the Turin–Milan main line at Santhià.

properties.name: Leamington–Stratford line
properties.highlight: The Stratford-on-Avon Railway opened its branch from Hatton on 9 October 1860; Chiltern trains still use it to reach Shakespeare’s town off the Birmingham–Oxford main line.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: The Louvain-to-Charleroi company opened its whole route in 1855, Leuven to Wavre in February and the last stretch into the Sambre coalfield that August; the IC-24 still runs it end to end.

properties.name: West Friesland line
properties.highlight: Schiphol and Amsterdam at one end, then the Hollandsche IJzeren’s branch of 1884 north through Purmerend into West Friesland, extended past Hoorn in 1885.

properties.name: Koleje Dolnośląskie D25
properties.highlight: Most of the old Breslau–Berlin trunk, in its 1875 alignment through Żagań: a single Lower Silesian sprinter crosses the Nysa at Zasieki and runs 189 km to Wrocław.

properties.name: EuroCity Via Regia
properties.highlight: Named for the medieval road it shadows: the EuroCity takes the Oberlausitz company’s line of 1874 and crosses at Horka, a border that carried no scheduled passenger trains for decades.

properties.name: LTG Link
properties.highlight: The old Tilsit–Memel line of 1875 along the edge of the Nemunas delta, joined at Klaipėda to the German military railway of 1915 up to Kretinga; trains came back to the Šilutė stretch in 2018.

properties.name: Mardi Gras Service
properties.highlight: The Gulf Coast’s first passenger trains since Hurricane Katrina: from August 2025 two a day have run from New Orleans along the Mississippi shore through Bay St. Louis, Gulfport and Biloxi to Mobile.

properties.name: Illinois Zephyr & Carl Sandburg
properties.highlight: America’s longest continuously running state-sponsored train: the Illinois Zephyr has run since November 1971, joined by the Carl Sandburg in 2006, across the prairie to Quincy on the Mississippi.

properties.name: VIA Senneterre
properties.highlight: A flag-stop train into the Abitibi bush three times a week: 13½ hours from Montreal past hunting and fishing clubs listed as request stops, to Senneterre, whose station opened in 1914.

properties.name: Wairarapa Connection
properties.highlight: Through the 8.8 km Remutaka Tunnel of 1955, New Zealand’s longest until 1978: rebuilt British Mark 2 carriages behind a KiwiRail diesel link Masterton and Wellington five times each weekday.

properties.name: Bairnsdale line
properties.highlight: Across Gippsland from Melbourne: three VLocity trains a day pass the Latrobe Valley’s coal towns to Bairnsdale, reached by rail in 1888; beyond Sale the trains stopped in 1993 and returned in 2004.

properties.name: Hunter Line
properties.highlight: Australia’s last regular steam passenger trains ran here until July 1971. Railcars now take the Hunter River Railway Company’s line of 1857 up the valley from Newcastle to Scone.

properties.name: Armidale Xplorer
properties.highlight: Up the Great Northern to the New England tableland, reached at Armidale in 1883: a daily Xplorer climbs eight hours from Sydney through the Hunter Valley and over the Liverpool Range.

properties.name: Kounotori
properties.highlight: Named in 2011 for the storks bred back into the wild at Toyooka: a limited express from Shin-Osaka through the Tamba hills and down the San’in line to the hot-spring town of Kinosaki.

properties.name: Etsumi-Hoku Line
properties.highlight: The Kuzuryū Line, completed in 1972: one-car KiHa 120s climb from Fukui through the castle town of Ōno to a dam lake, the last stretch still worked with a single staff, one of two left on JR.

properties.name: AREX Express
properties.highlight: Non-stop since December 2010 from Seoul Station, where some airlines check passengers in and through immigration, to Incheon Airport over the lower deck of the Yeongjong Bridge.

properties.name: Banja Luka–Doboj railway
properties.highlight: One of the last lines built by Yugoslavia’s youth work brigades, opened in 1951, from Banja Luka up the Vrbanja valley to Doboj. Rebuilt for 120 km/h in 2018; a daily train since December 2025.

properties.name: Macomer–Nuoro railway
properties.highlight: Nuoro’s only railway: the narrow-gauge line reached the town in February 1889, and ARST railcars still run down it to the main line at Macomer several times each weekday.

properties.name: Banyubiru
properties.highlight: On Indonesia’s first railway: the Dutch NIS company’s line out of Semarang reached Solo in February 1870, and the Banyubiru runs it twice a day through Gundih between Solo Balapan and Semarang Tawang.

properties.name: Batara Kresna Railbus
properties.highlight: Down the middle of Solo’s main street on an old tramway’s track, then out on the extension of 1922 to Wonogiri; since February 2025 a faster railcar takes about an hour, not two.

properties.name: Varna–Dobrich railway
properties.highlight: Built to carry Dobruja’s harvest to the sea: the branch from Devnya reached Dobrich in 1910, and five BDŽ trains a day still link the town with the port of Varna.

properties.name: Nador–Taourirt line
properties.highlight: Opened by King Mohammed VI in July 2009: a new railway from the port of Beni Ensar, under Nador in a 3 km tunnel and south across the plain to Taourirt on the Fez–Oujda main line.

properties.name: IC Łempicka
properties.highlight: Lublin to Wrocław the long way round, through Radom, Kielce and Częstochowa, then west across Silesia to Opole and the Oder; the Częstochowa to Kielce link, opened in 1911, was the last piece of the route.

properties.name: IC Kasztelan
properties.highlight: Kraków to Hrubieszów near the Ukrainian border, by Tarnów, Mielec and Stalowa Wola, then east through Biłgoraj and Zwierzyniec to Zamość and its Renaissance old town; the line from Stalowa Wola to Biłgoraj was only completed in 1976.

properties.name: Intercity
properties.highlight: From Poperinge’s hop fields through Ypres, then along the French border by Wervik and Menen to Kortrijk, Ghent and Antwerp; the last link, the rail tunnel under the Scheldt, opened in 1970.

properties.name: Palermo–Catania railway
properties.highlight: Across the middle of Sicily from Catania, up by Enna and the old sulphur country of Caltanissetta and down to the Tyrrhenian coast at Palermo; the line was complete only when the Marianopoli tunnel opened in 1885.

properties.name: RE 7 Erfurt–Würzburg
properties.highlight: From Erfurt over the Thuringian Forest through the 3 km Brandleite tunnel under the Rennsteig, down by Suhl and Grimmenthal into Franconia and on by Schweinfurt to Würzburg; the climb and the tunnel opened in 1884.

properties.name: Glasgow South Western Line
properties.highlight: The other line from Carlisle to Glasgow: over the border at Gretna, by Annan and Dumfries, up Nithsdale to Kilmarnock, and in by Barrhead on the joint line opened in 1873.

properties.name: Franz-Josefs-Bahn
properties.highlight: Vienna’s line to the Waldviertel: from the Franz-Josefs-Bahnhof along the Danube to Tulln, up by Eggenburg and across the forest plateau to Gmünd and over the Czech border to České Velenice; the Vienna end opened in 1870.

properties.name: West of England line
properties.highlight: The other way to Exeter: from Waterloo by Woking and Basingstoke, then west by Andover, Salisbury, Sherborne and Yeovil Junction, much of it on single track, to Exeter Central and down to St Davids, reached in 1862.

properties.name: Stranraer line
properties.highlight: From Stranraer on Loch Ryan over the moors by Barrhill, the only station left between there and Girvan, then along the Firth of Clyde by Ayr and Troon to Kilmarnock; the line through the hills opened in 1877.

properties.name: Padua–Belluno railway
properties.highlight: From Padua across the Venetian plain by Castelfranco and Montebelluna into the Piave valley at Feltre and on to Belluno beneath the Dolomites; the line that gave Belluno its railway opened on 10 November 1886.

properties.name: RE 3 Saarbrücken–Frankfurt
properties.highlight: From Saarbrücken by Neunkirchen and St. Wendel down the Nahe valley past Idar-Oberstein and Kirn to Bad Kreuznach, then along the Rhine to Mainz and over to Frankfurt; the Nahe valley railway was complete in 1860.

properties.name: Pau–Bedous railway
properties.highlight: From Pau by Oloron-Sainte-Marie up the Aspe valley into the Pyrenees to Bedous, the first stretch of the old line to Canfranc and Spain; trains reached Bedous in 1914, stopped in 1980 and came back on 26 June 2016.

properties.name: Bayonne–Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port railway
properties.highlight: Up the Nive valley from Bayonne by Cambo-les-Bains into the Basque hills to Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, where pilgrims set out over the Pyrenees to Roncesvalles; the last stretch, from Ossès, opened on 11 December 1898.

properties.name: RB 55 Munich–Bayrischzell
properties.highlight: The Bayerische Regiobahn from Munich by Holzkirchen to the shore of the Schliersee and up the Leitzach valley under the Wendelstein to Bayrischzell; the last stretch, from Fischbachau, opened on 1 October 1911.

properties.name: Yorkshire Coast Line
properties.highlight: From Hull by Beverley and Driffield to Bridlington, then along the Yorkshire coast by Filey to Scarborough; the last link, from Bridlington to Filey, opened on 20 October 1847.

properties.name: Hastings line
properties.highlight: From Charing Cross through the North Downs by the Sevenoaks tunnel to Tonbridge, then over the High Weald by Tunbridge Wells and Battle to the sea at Hastings; London trains have run this way since the Sevenoaks line opened in 1868.

properties.name: Limoges–Ussel railway
properties.highlight: From Limoges up the Vienne valley by Eymoutiers onto the Plateau de Millevaches, the high moorland of the Limousin, and down by Meymac to Ussel; the stretch from Eymoutiers to Meymac, opened on 8 October 1883, completed the line.

properties.name: RE 5 Cuxhaven–Hamburg
properties.highlight: Along the lower Elbe from the North Sea port of Cuxhaven by Otterndorf, Stade and Buxtehude to Harburg and over the river into Hamburg; the railway reached Cuxhaven in 1881.

properties.name: Svendborgbanen
properties.highlight: Across Funen from Svendborg, the harbour for the ferries to Ærø and the small islands of the South Funen archipelago, by Kværndrup and Ringe to Odense; the line opened in July 1876.

properties.name: Givet–Charleville railway
properties.highlight: Up the Meuse through the Ardennes from Givet, at the tip of the French salient into Belgium, by Fumay, Revin and Nouzonville to Charleville-Mézières; the line reached Givet on 28 April 1862.

properties.name: Empire Builder (Portland section)
properties.highlight: The Empire Builder’s Portland half: it leaves the Seattle cars at Spokane in the night and follows the Columbia River from Pasco down its gorge to Portland, a section Amtrak brought back in 1981.

properties.name: Lake Shore Limited (Boston section)
properties.highlight: The Lake Shore Limited’s Boston cars, split from the New York train at Albany–Rensselaer, cross the Berkshires by Pittsfield and Springfield on the old Boston and Albany; first run in 1975.

properties.name: Northeast Regional (Roanoke)
properties.highlight: From Boston down the whole Northeast Corridor, then past Washington by Charlottesville and Lynchburg to Roanoke, where the Northeast Regional, paid for by Virginia, brought trains back in 2017.
